### Emoji in `[brackets]`

-   `[any emoji]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the repository
-   `[number]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the file
-   `[🧠]` Marks a place where there is something to decide and think about.
-   `[🕕]` List of models _(that should be progresively updated)_
    -   Prompt: Update available models and their prices, search online
-   `[🔼]` Marks an entity (function, class, type,...) in other project (like Promptbook.studio) which should be moved to this repository
-   `[🚉]` Marks an types / interfaces / structures fully serializable as JSON, not marking `string_` and `number_` prefixed aliases
-   `[🧹]` Need to implement garbage collection
-   `[🐣]` Easter eggs
-   `[💩]` Shitty code that needs refactoring
-   `$` When entity (function, class) starts by `$`, it means it is not pure and can have side effects.
-   3x `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed before releasing a pre-release version.
-   4x (and more) `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed as soon as possible.
-   `@@@` Marks a place where text / documentation / ... must be written.
-   [⚫] Code in this file should never be published in any package
-   [🟢] Code in this file should never be published into packages that could be imported into browser environment
-   [🔵] Code in this file should never be published outside of `@promptbook/browser`
-   [🟡] Code in this file should never be published outside of `@promptbook/cli`
-   [💞] Ignore a discrepancy between file name and entity name

### Dictionary

-   **Promptbook Engine vs. Agent Server** sre two distinct parts you should know the difference:
    -   **Promptbook Engine** is the core engine that powers AI agents, it is located in `/src` folder. It is framework-agnostic and can be used in different applications. It can run as standalone javascript/typescript library, CLI environment, or be integrated into different applications. It can be also runned in Agent Server:
    -   **Agent Server** is a specific application that uses the Promptbook Engine to provide a web and API interface for creating and interacting with AI agents. It is located in `/apps/agents-server` folder.
-   **Commitments** are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents
    -   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, etc.
    -   Commitments are in the folder `/src/commitments`
    -   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g., `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a begining of the line and end by new co
    -   Agent source with commitments is parsed by two functions:
        -   `parseAgentSource` which is a lightweight parser for agent source, it parses basic information and its purpose is to be quick and synchronous. The commitments there are hardcoded.
        -   `createAgentModelRequirements` which is an asynchronous function that creates model requirements it applies each commitment one by one and works asynchronously.

#### Agents server installed on VPS _(as additional context)_

-   There are two distinct things:
    1. Entire VPS
    2. Each server
-   On one VPS there can be multiple servers and each server has its own domain
-   Most things (like agents, projects, metadata, etc.) are living on each server and some things (like environment variables, superadmin, etc.) are bound to entire VPS
-   Purpose of this is to be able to run multiple clients on one VPS and each client can have its own server with its own domain and settings
-   The entire VPS is managed by superadmin and each server is managed by normal admin of that server _(or superadmin can also manage each server)_
-   Superadmin has always name `admin` and password hardcoded in environment variable `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
-   The VPS is installed by running [the `install.sh`](install.sh) script on a fresh VPS
-   Servers can be added and removed by superadmin on `/superadmin/servers` page

#### The Agents Server menu _(as additional context)_

The menu of the agent server looks like this:

1. The navigation hierarchy
    - Icon and Server name _(for example Promptbook Agents Server)_
    - arrow ">" and Agents or picked agent name (organized in folders)
    - arrow ">" and the view Profile / Chat / Book of the agent or nothing if no agent is picked
2. The menu items
    - Documentation
    - System
3. Control panel and user menu
    - Control panel
    - User menu with the avatar and the name of the user

#### Database migrations for Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   Migrations are located in `apps/agents-server/src/database/migrations`
-   Be aware that table names in migrations have prefix `prefix_` _(look at existing migrations for reference)_
-   Migrations should be backwards compatible:
    -   Meaning that earlier versions of the server should be able to run with the database after migration without any issues.
    -   This is important because we want to have the same database for production and preview environments.
    -   This database will be migrated to the latest version of the preview environment, but the production environment should be able to run with it without any issues.
    -   The only thing that can happen is that older versions of the server will not be able to use new features.
    -   Adding new columns, tables, etc. is fine, but do not remove or rename existing ones, and do not change the meaning of existing columns or tables.
    -   When in doubt, prefer to add new things instead of changing existing ones.

#### Metadata of Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   There is a table called `Metadata`.
-   It has `key` and `value` fields.
-   It is a similar concept to configuration, but this configuration can be changed by administrators in the Agents Server website.

#### Book Language blueprint _(as additional context)_

Book language is a domain-specific language used for defining AI agents in the Promptbook Engine and Agents server.
It has lightweight syntax and keywords (the commitments) that allow you to define the "soul" of the agent.
The book language is designed to be human-readable and easy to write, while also being powerful enough to express complex agent behaviors.

Every agent has its source defined in the book language, which is called "agent source". The agent source is parsed and processed by the Promptbook Engine to create the actual AI agent that can interact with users and perform tasks.
This agent source is internally converted to a structured format called "agent model requirements" which are the actual raw technical instructions for the AI model to run the agent.

There is a standalone book language documentation on each agent server on `/api/docs/book.md` route, for example `https://live.ptbk.io/api/docs/book-language.md?language=en`.
Use it as a reference for the syntax and semantics of the book language, and modify `apps/agents-server/src/utils/bookLanguageDocumentation/createStandaloneBookLanguageMarkdown.ts` if it is relevant to the change you are doing.

##### Commitments _(as additional context and part of Book Language)_

Commitments are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents written in `book` language.

-   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, `CLOSED`, etc.
-   They are in the folder `src/commitments`.
-   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g. `PERSONA`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a beginning of the line and ends by a new commitment or the end of the book.
-   There is a general pattern that the commitment keyword is followed by a space and then by the content of the commitment, for example:
    -   `PERSONA You are a helpful assistant that helps with cooking recipes.`
    -   `USE MCP https://mcp.example.com/server`
-   In the commitment context, you can reference external agents, for example:
    -   `TEAM You can talk to {Criminal lawyer} and {Financial advisor}`

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01RW7uX6iiu6dp54LzqSMzsd","type":"tool_result","content":"-   Added an in-progress signal to `ptbk coder`. A prompt used to jump straight from not started `[ ]` to fully implemented `[x]`, so a queue running for hours never showed which task was being worked on and a coder which was killed or crashed left no trace of the interrupted task at all. Now the prompt file itself carries the intermediate `[^]` status, which is rewritten before every single step of the round, so it always names the harness, the model, the thinking level, the steps which already finished with their price and duration, and the step which is running right now — for example `` [^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` - Implementation in progress ``, then `` [^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing in progress ``, and finally the unchanged `` [x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes ``. Only the verified `[x]` state is committed, because the round commit is still created after the prompt has been implemented and verified. The `[^]` status is deliberately never reverted: a killed process, an internal error or any other interruption leaves it in the prompt file as the signal that this task was left in the middle, and such a prompt is not picked up again automatically. The in-progress and the done status lines are built from one shared formatter, so they can never drift apart; the `ptbk coder server` board shows a left-behind `[^]` prompt in its **In progress** column with a `[^]` tag, and `ptbk coder verify` no longer offers a file containing an interrupted prompt for archiving. Because the harness reports its authentication method only when a step finishes, the `(ChatGPT account)` part appears as soon as the first coding step is done. The `ptbk coder` landing page documents the new status.\n\n-   Added a running indicator to the Agents Server **System** menu. While a standalone VPS self-update is in progress, the **Super Admin → Update** entry is now decorated with small spinning arrows, so a super admin sees a running update straight from the menu instead of having to open `/superadmin/update`. The indicator follows the same route-based registry pattern as the existing administrator warning triangles: one shared indicator renderer now draws both the warning and the running state, and the running state is resolved server-side only for the super admin, so nobody else learns about VPS operations. Whether a self-update is really in progress is decided by one shared `isVpsSelfUpdateJobRunning` check, which the update launcher and the installed-version cleanup use as well, so a job whose installer process died without writing its final status is not reported as running.\n\n-   **Breaking:** Removed the `COMPONENT`, `WALLET` / `WALLETS`, `MEMORY` / `MEMORIES`, `USE BROWSER`, `USE DEEPSEARCH`, `USE SEARCH ENGINE`, `USE SPAWN`, `USE TIMEOUT`, `USE TIME`, `USE EMAIL` and generic `META` commitments from the Book language without any backwards compatibility. `COMPONENT` describes the UI that runs the agent, and wallet, memory, browsing, deep search, web search, timeouts, current time, and e-mail are capabilities of the Agent Server which every agent gets anyway, so none of them belongs in the agent source; `USE SPAWN` was unused. The commitment folders, their tool definitions, tool functions, runtime adapters and system-message aggregation were deleted, together with the `USE` system-message aggregation step, the browser / search / e-mail / timeout / memory / wallet **agent capabilities** shown on agent profiles, the matching entries of the New agent wizard (including its e-mail setup step and translations), and the `USE EMAIL` extraction which the Agent Server used to derive per-agent e-mail configuration from the agent source — e-mail sending is now resolved for every agent from the [user wallet](apps/agents-server/src/utils/useEmailSmtpWalletConstants.ts) alone. The generic `META <TYPE> <content>` catch-all is gone as well: only concrete `META` commitments are commitments now, so `META TITLE`, `META AUTHOR` or any other free-form `META` line is no longer parsed. Because of that, `META DESCRIPTION` (whose definition already existed but was never registered), `META FULLNAME` and the low-level `META ID` are now first-class commitments with their own definitions, which keeps agent descriptions, display names, and permanent ids working exactly as before. `fetchUrlContent` moved from the `USE BROWSER` commitment to [`src/scrapers/_common/utils/fetchUrlContent.ts`](src/scrapers/_common/utils/fetchUrlContent.ts) because it is a scraping utility used by the Agent Server `run_browser` tool and the `/api/scrape` route, and the Agent Server keeps all of its own runtime features — the browser tool, `send_email`, `spawn_agent`, user memory, user wallet, and chat timeouts — since they are server functionality rather than agent source syntax. The Book language documentation, the standalone Book language markdown, the commitment dictionary, the specs, the READMEs, the VSCode grammar, and the bundled default agent books were updated accordingly.\n\n-   Added the `N*M` notation to `--count` of `ptbk coder generate-boilerplates`, which now controls not only how many prompt files are generated but also how many prompts are written into each of them. `--count 10*7` creates 10 files with 7 prompts each, while a plain `--count 10` keeps the previous meaning and is treated as `--count 10*1`. The default is `5*1`, so one generated file contains exactly one prompt instead of the four identical copies it used to contain, and the `coder:generate-boilerplates` script which `ptbk coder init` writes into `package.json` uses `--count 5*1` as well. More than one prompt per file is an advanced option: every single generated prompt is one separate coding task, so each of them is separated by a `---` line and reserves **its own fresh emoji tag** instead of sharing one tag with the rest of the file. A `--count` value which is not one or two positive integers is now refused with an actionable error instead of silently falling back to 5 files, the `--count` parsing is shared by the CLI command and the `generate-prompt-boilerplate` repository script, and the `ptbk coder` landing page lists the new notation among the advanced features.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder ping`, which sends one tiny dummy prompt through a selected harness and model — for example `ptbk coder ping --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.6-sol --thinking-level xhigh` — and reports the answer of the harness, the measured response time and the usage the harness reported for it. The ping is built on the very same runner the coding queue uses, so it really exercises the configured harness, model, thinking level and authentication (including the rate-limit retry behavior) instead of only checking that the harness command is installed. Besides testing that a connection works and how fast it answers, it is meant to be run **before** you actually need the harness: the tiny prompt starts the hourly/weekly quota window, so the refresh clock is already running by the time the real coding starts. The dummy work needs no tool and explicitly forbids reading, writing or changing anything, and both temporary artifacts the ping creates are removed again, so the project is left exactly as it was — nothing is written, changed or committed. `--no-ui` streams the raw harness output instead of the compact result, and `--allow-credits` behaves as in `ptbk coder run`. The `ptbk coder` landing page documents the new command among the advanced features.\n\n-   Added `--commit`, `--auto-push` and `--auto-pull` to `ptbk coder init`, `ptbk coder add`, `ptbk coder generate-boilerplates` and `ptbk coder verify`. These commands change project files but used to leave the result uncommitted; now `--auto-pull` pulls the latest changes before the command changes anything, `--commit` commits what the command created with the coding-agent git identity, and `--auto-push` pushes that commit to the remote repository. `ptbk coder verify` applies the synchronization around each single verification, so archiving a finished prompt file and appending a repair prompt are committed and pushed one by one instead of at the end of the whole session. All four commands share one implementation of the pulling, committing and pushing, a repository without any change is never committed as an empty commit, and `--auto-push` without `--commit` is refused with an actionable error. `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server`, which already commit every successful round by default, are unchanged. As part of this, the temporary commit message file which `ptbk coder` writes inside the project is now always kept out of the created commit, so a project which does not keep the Promptbook temporary directory out of version control is no longer left with a dirty working tree after committing.\n\n-   Optimized the startup time of the `ptbk` CLI utility. Simply running `ptbk about` used to take several seconds because the published bundle eagerly loaded the heavy third-party dependencies of the whole engine — `jsdom`, `@mozilla/readability`, `@openai/agents`, `openai`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@azure/openai`, `jszip`, `socket.io-client` and `prompts` — even for commands that never touch them. These packages are now imported on first use through one shared `createLazyModuleLoader` utility, so a command pays for a dependency only when it really uses it; the repository scripts load `typescript` and `pg` the same way. Every command, option and output stays exactly the same; the website scraper, the OpenAI AgentKit tools, the LLM providers, the `.bookc` archive reader/writer, the remote client and the interactive prompts just load their SDK at the moment they need it. Measured on the generated `@promptbook/cli` bundle, `ptbk about` dropped from about 4.6 s to about 1.8 s, which is roughly 2.8 s saved on every single `ptbk` invocation.\n\n-   Optimized standalone Agents Server self-updates. The request-aware root layout now declares its dynamic boundary before static prerendering can start database-backed work, CLI-owned release builds no longer write unusable multi-gigabyte webpack filesystem caches, retained release caches are reclaimed before deployment, and each update phase records its elapsed time in the installer log.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server ElevenLabs text-to-speech configuration to use only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`; support for the legacy `ELEVEN_LABS_API_KEY` environment variable was removed.\n\n-   Added `--test-before <no|yes-and-fail|yes-and-fix>` to `ptbk coder run`. Pre-coding verification is disabled by default, can stop the run with the complete test output when existing tests fail, or can create and run one shared-format repair prompt before the normal coding queue; an explicit `--test` command is used when provided and `npm test` is the default for the enabled modes. The Coder landing page and local VS Code coder terminals now document and use the repair mode.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"74608ceb-c452-4e82-b385-4ad6b325ff5b","uuid":"17a63185-c310-4aa2-8805-98d431961d01","timestamp":"2026-09-17T16:17:55.705Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"-   Added an in-progress signal to `ptbk coder`. command in the CLI\n *\n * @private internal function of `promptbookCli`\n */\nexport function $initializeCoderRunCommand(program: Program): $side_effect {\n    const command = program.command('run');\n    command.description(\n        spaceTrim(\n            (block) => `\n            Execute coding prompts through selected AI agent\n\n            ${block(PROMPT_RUNNER_DESCRIPTION)}\n\n            ${block(QUESTIONS_DESCRIPTION)}\n\n            Features:\n            - Resolves FROM, IMPORT and TEAM by agent name, book-relative path, project path or URL\n            - Creates a missing .core/adam.book beside the selected agent for default inheritance\n            - Automatically stages and commits changes with agent identity unless --no-commit is used\n            - Commits only the prompt file and the files the coding agent has changed, leaving unrelated changes alone\n            - Refuses to start on a dirty working tree unless --git-changes says what should happen with the changes\n            - Optional --git-changes continue resumes the single prompt an interrupted coder left in the [^] status\n            - Optional post-commit git push with explicit --auto-push opt-in\n            - Optional pre-prompt git pull with explicit --auto-pull opt-in\n            - Optional --isolate runs every prompt in its own temporary git worktree and merges it back when verified\n            - Saves the run trace of every round into prompts/traces/, named after its prompt file\n            - Optional --preserve-logs keeps temp prompt/log artifacts after successful rounds\n            - Optional --no-ui keeps plain streaming console output for logging and debugging\n            - Refuses to start on a nearly full disk and pauses the run when the free disk space becomes critical, unless --no-questions is used\n            - Checks that the selected harness is installed and up to date before the first prompt unless --no-questions is used\n            - Offers to add missing project-local ignore rules for the selected harness\n            - In interactive mode, checks local and global Promptbook CLI installations and offers to update them\n            - Supports GPG signing of commits\n            - Optional pre-coding test run that can stop or repair pre-existing failures\n            - Optional post-prompt verification with test-feedback retries\n            - Progress tracking and interactive P/S/X terminal controls\n            - Dry-run mode to preview prompts\n        `,\n        ),\n    );\n\n    command.option('--dry-run', 'Print unwritten prompts without executing', false);\n    addPromptRunnerSelectionOptions(command);\n    addQuestionsOption(command);\n    addCoderAgentOption(command);\n    command.option(\n        '--context <context-or-file>',\n        'Append extra instructions either inline or from a file path relative to the current project',\n    );\n    command.option(\n        '--test <test-command...>',\n        'Run a verification command after each prompt; quote it when the command itself contains top-level flags',\n    );\n    command.addOption(\n        new Option(\n            '--test-before <mode>',\n            `Run tests before coding: ${TEST_BEFORE_MODE_VALUES.join(\n                ', ',\n            )} (defaults to no; uses npm test when --test is omitted)`,\n        )\n            .choices([...TEST_BEFORE_MODE_VALUES])\n            .default('no'),\n    );\n    command.option(\n        '--preserve-logs',\n        'Keep generated temp prompt/log artifacts after successful rounds for debugging and analytics',\n        false,\n    );\n    addPromptRunnerExecutionOptions(command);\n    command.option(\n        '--isolate',\n        spaceTrim(`\n            Implement each prompt in its own temporary git worktree with its own isolated environment.\n            A verified task is merged back into the branch the coder runs on and the worktree is deleted.\n            A task that cannot be merged is marked as failed and its worktree is kept for a manual merge.\n        `),\n        false,\n    );\n    addPromptPriorityOptions(command);\n    command.option(\n        '--limit <run-count>',\n        'Stop after processing this many prompt runs',\n        createPositiveIntegerOptionParser('--limit'),\n    );\n    command.option(\n        '--wait-after-prompt <duration>',\n        spaceTrim(`\n            Wait this long after each prompt has been implemented, verified and committed before starting the next prompt.\n            Accepts durations like 1h, 30m, 5s. Defaults to 0 (no wait).\n        `),\n    );\n    command.option(\n        '--wait-between-prompts <duration>',\n        spaceTrim(`\n            Pace prompts so that each next prompt starts at least this long after the previous one began.\n            If the previous prompt already took longer than this, the next prompt starts immediately.\n            Accepts durations like 1h, 30m, 5s. Defaults to 0 (no pacing).\n        `),\n    );\n    command.option(\n        '--wait-after-error <duration>',\n        spaceTrim(`\n            Wait this long before retrying a prompt after an error occurs (up to 3 retries before giving up).\n            Accepts durations like 1h, 30m, 5s. Defaults to 10m.\n        `),\n    );\n    // Note: --no-auto disables the default auto behaviour and waits for user confirmation before each prompt\n    command.option(\n        '--no-auto',\n        'Wait for user confirmation before each prompt instead of running automatically through the queue',\n    );\n    command.option(\n        '--auto-migrate',\n        'Run testing-server database migrations automatically after each successfully processed prompt',\n    );\n    command.option(\n        '--allow-destructive-auto-migrate',\n        'Allow auto-migrate even when heuristic SQL safety check flags destructive pending migrations',\n    );\n\n    command.action(\n        handleActionErrors(async (cliOptions) => {\n            const {\n                dryRun,\n                agent,\n                context,\n                test,\n                testBefore,\n                preserveLogs,\n                isolate: isIsolated,\n                priority,\n                minPriority: minimumPriority,\n                maxPriority: maximumPriority,\n                limit,\n                waitAfterPrompt: waitAfterPromptValue,\n                waitBetweenPrompts: waitBetweenPromptsValue,\n                waitAfterError: waitAfterErrorValue,\n                auto,\n                autoMigrate,\n                allowDestructiveAutoMigrate,\n            } = cliOptions as {\n                readonly dryRun: boolean;\n                readonly agent?: string;\n                readonly context?: string;\n                readonly test?: string | string[];\n                readonly testBefore: TestBeforeMode;\n                readonly preserveLogs: boolean;\n                readonly isolate: boolean;\n                readonly priority?: number;\n                readonly minPriority?: number;\n                readonly maxPriority?: number;\n                readonly limit?: number;\n                readonly waitAfterPrompt?: string;\n                readonly waitBetweenPrompts?: string;\n                readonly waitAfterError?: string;\n                readonly auto: boolean;\n                readonly autoMigrate: boolean;\n                readonly allowDestructiveAutoMigrate: boolean;\n            } & PromptRunnerCliOptions &\n                CoderAgentCliOptions;\n\n            const configuredTestCommand = normalizeCommandOptionValue(test);\n            const testCommand = configuredTestCommand ?? (testBefore === 'no' ? undefined : DEFAULT_CODER_TEST_COMMAND);\n            const runnerOptions = normalizePromptRunnerCliOptions(cliOptions as PromptRunnerCliOptions, {\n                isAgentRequired: !dryRun,\n            });\n            const questionsOptions = normalizeQuestionsCliOptions(cliOptions as QuestionsCliOptions);\n\n            // [1] Parse the wait options and --no-auto:\n            //   default: run automatically through the queue (no waiting between prompts)\n            //   --no-auto: wait for user confirmation before each prompt (interactive mode)\n            //   --wait-after-prompt: pause after a successful round before starting the next prompt\n            //   --wait-between-prompts: pace from start of one prompt to start of next\n            //   --wait-after-error: wait before retrying after an error (default 10m)\n            const waitForUser = !auto;\n\n            assertUserConfirmationIsAllowed({ ...questionsOptions, isWaitingForUser: waitForUser });\n\n            // Note: Checked before anything is installed or written, because installing a harness, updating the\n            //       Promptbook CLI and coding itself all need the disk space which is missing\n            await $assertSufficientFreeDiskSpace(process.cwd());\n\n            if (await $ensurePromptbookCliInstallations(questionsOptions)) {\n                return process.exit(0);\n            }\n\n            await $ensureHarnessInstallations([runnerOptions.agentName], questionsOptions);\n            await $ensureCoderHarnessGitignoreRules(process.cwd(), runnerOptions.agentName, questionsOptions);\n\n            const waitAfterPrompt = parseOptionalWaitDuration(waitAfterPromptValue, 0);\n            const waitBetweenPrompts = parseOptionalWaitDuration(waitBetweenPromptsValue, 0);\n            const waitAfterError = parseOptionalWaitDuration(waitAfterErrorValue, DEFAULT_WAIT_AFTER_ERROR_MS);\n\n            // Convert commander options to RunOptions format\n            const runOptions = {\n                dryRun,\n                waitForUser,\n                waitAfterPrompt,\n                waitBetweenPrompts,\n                waitAfterError,\n                noCommit: runnerOptions.noCommit,\n                gitChanges: runnerOptions.gitChanges,\n                agentName: preserveLogs,\n                isIsolated,\n                noUi: runnerOptions.noUi,\n                thinkingLevel: runnerOptions.thinkingLevel,\n                priority: priority ?? 0,\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01J8Mr1jNmaCRJW6JnarWdG3","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport type { PromptRunner } from '../runners/types/PromptRunner';\n2\timport type { CoderRunUiState } from './CoderRunUiState';\n3\t\n4\t/**\n5\t * Refreshes optional harness subscription usage in the shared coder-run UI state.\n6\t *\n7\t * Subscription visibility is an enhancement, not a prerequisite for running prompts. A harness which cannot expose a\n8\t * snapshot, or whose account endpoint is temporarily unavailable, therefore leaves the existing dashboard unchanged.\n9\t *\n10\t * @private internal utility of coder run UI\n11\t */\n12\texport async function refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage(options: {\n13\t    readonly runner: PromptRunner;\n14\t    readonly uiState: CoderRunUiState | undefined;\n15\t}): Promise<void> {\n16\t    const { runner, uiState } = options;\n17\t\n18\t    if (!uiState || !runner.getSubscriptionUsage) {\n19\t        return;\n20\t    }\n21\t\n22\t    try {\n23\t        const subscriptionUsage = await runner.getSubscriptionUsage();\n24\t\n25\t        if (subscriptionUsage) {\n26\t            uiState.setSubscriptionUsage(subscriptionUsage);\n27\t        }\n28\t    } catch {\n29\t        // A current subscription snapshot must never interrupt the coding queue.\n30\t    }\n31\t}\n32\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"74608ceb-c452-4e82-b385-4ad6b325ff5b","uuid":"9bddbab6-85b2-4928-b1bc-9ade997fffe3","timestamp":"2026-09-17T16:18:19.765Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\ai\\promptbook\\scripts\\run-codex-prompts\\ui\\refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage.ts","content":"import type { PromptRunner } from '../runners/types/PromptRunner';\nimport type { CoderRunUiState } from './CoderRunUiState';\n\n/**\n * Refreshes optional harness subscription usage in the shared coder-run UI state.\n *\n * Subscription visibility is an enhancement, not a prerequisite for running prompts. A harness which cannot expose a\n * snapshot, or whose account endpoint is temporarily unavailable, therefore leaves the existing dashboard unchanged.\n *\n * @private internal utility of coder run UI\n */\nexport async function refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage(options: {\n    readonly runner: PromptRunner;\n    readonly uiState: CoderRunUiState | undefined;\n}): Promise<void> {\n    const { runner, uiState } = options;\n\n    if (!uiState || !runner.getSubscriptionUsage) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const subscriptionUsage = await runner.getSubscriptionUsage();\n\n        if (subscriptionUsage) {\n            uiState.setSubscriptionUsage(subscriptionUsage);\n        }\n    } catch {\n        // A current subscription snapshot must never interrupt the coding queue.\n    }\n}\n","numLines":32,"startLine":1,"totalLines":32}}}

(lines.length === 0) {\n            return;\n        }\n        this.agentOutputLines.push(...lines);\n        if (this.agentOutputLines.length > MAX_AGENT_OUTPUT_LINES) {\n            this.agentOutputLines = this.agentOutputLines.slice(-MAX_AGENT_OUTPUT_LINES);\n        }\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Transitions the execution phase shown in the UI.\n     */\n    public setPhase(phase: CoderRunPhase): void {\n        this.phase = phase;\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Updates the status message line beneath the current prompt label.\n     */\n    public setStatusMessage(message: string): void {\n        this.statusMessage = message;\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Replaces the contextual detail lines shown beneath the current prompt status.\n     */\n    public setDetailLines(detailLines: string[]): void {\n        this.detailLines = detailLines.filter((detailLine) => detailLine.trim() !== '');\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Replaces the exact user-message preview lines shown in agent-specific panels.\n     */\n    public setMessagePreviewLines(messagePreviewLines: string[]): void {\n        this.messagePreviewLines = [...messagePreviewLines];\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Replaces the structured user-message panels shown in agent-specific dashboards.\n     */\n    public setMessagePreviewSections(messagePreviewSections: AgentRunMessagePreviewSection[]): void {\n        this.messagePreviewSections = [...messagePreviewSections];\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Replaces agent status rows shown by agent-specific terminal frames.\n     */\n    public setAgentStatusLines(agentStatusLines: string[]): void {\n        this.agentStatusLines = [...agentStatusLines];\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Replaces structured agent status rows shown by agent-specific terminal frames.\n     */\n    public setAgentStatusTableRows(agentStatusTableRows: AgentRunStatusTableRow[]): void {\n        this.agentStatusTableRows = [...agentStatusTableRows];\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Replaces the optional harness subscription usage shown in the Session box.\n     */\n    public setSubscriptionUsage(subscriptionUsage: HarnessSubscriptionUsage): void {\n        this.subscriptionUsage = subscriptionUsage;\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Sets or clears the Enter-key action label shown in the controls panel.\n     */\n    public setPendingEnterLabel(pendingEnterLabel: string | undefined): void {\n        this.pendingEnterLabel = pendingEnterLabel;\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Shows the answer of the runner to one pressed control key, or clears the currently shown one.\n     *\n     * Pressing one control twice in a row can produce the very same answer, for example when there is\n     * nothing to skip. The repeat count is therefore tracked here, so that even such a press changes the\n     * rendered frame and the user always sees that the key arrived.\n     */\n    public setControlFeedback(controlFeedback: CoderRunControlFeedback | undefined): void {\n        this.controlFeedback =\n            controlFeedback === undefined\n                ? undefined\n                : { ...controlFeedback, repeatCount: this.countControlFeedbackRepeat(controlFeedback) };\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Appends an error message to the error list shown in the UI.\n     */\n    public addError(errorMessage: string): void {\n        this.errors.push(errorMessage);\n        this.emitChange();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Counts how many times the shown answer repeats the previously shown one.\n     */\n    private countControlFeedbackRepeat(controlFeedback: CoderRunControlFeedback): number {\n        const previousControlFeedback = this.controlFeedback;\n        const isSameControlFeedback =\n            previousControlFeedback !== undefined &&\n            previousControlFeedback.controlKey === controlFeedback.controlKey &&\n            previousControlFeedback.message === controlFeedback.message;\n\n        return isSameControlFeedback ? previousControlFeedback.repeatCount + 1 : 1;\n    }\n\n    private emitChange(): void {\n        this.emit('change');\n    }\n}\n","numLines":330,"startLine":1,"totalLines":330}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GZNFDfR5u4nQCzViYSSzZK","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t/**\n2\t * One rolling subscription limit reported by a coding harness.\n3\t *\n4\t * @private internal type of `ptbk coder`\n5\t */\n6\texport type HarnessSubscriptionUsageLimit = {\n7\t    /**\n8\t     * Short, user-facing name of the limit window, for example `5h` or `7d`.\n9\t     */\n10\t    readonly label: string;\n11\t\n12\t    /**\n13\t     * Percentage of this limit which has already been consumed, from 0 through 100.\n14\t     */\n15\t    readonly usedPercentage: number;\n16\t\n17\t    /**\n18\t     * Unix timestamp in seconds at which this limit window resets, when reported by the harness.\n19\t     */\n20\t    readonly resetsAt?: number;\n21\t};\n22\t\n23\t/**\n24\t * Subscription usage snapshot which a coding harness can optionally report.\n25\t *\n26\t * The runner contract deliberately keeps this independent from per-prompt token usage: subscription limits can be\n27\t * shared with other tools and can contain several rolling windows.\n28\t *\n29\t * @private internal type of `ptbk coder`\n30\t */\n31\texport type HarnessSubscriptionUsage = {\n32\t    /**\n33\t     * Every subscription limit currently reported by the harness, in display order.\n34\t     */\n35\t    readonly limits: ReadonlyArray<HarnessSubscriptionUsageLimit>;\n36\t};\n37\t\n38\t/**\n39\t * Merges a newly reported subset of subscription windows into the latest complete snapshot.\n40\t *\n41\t * Some harnesses emit an update only for the limit whose state changed. Keeping the previous windows means a\n42\t * five-hour update cannot make a still-valid weekly limit disappear from the dashboard. Existing order is preserved\n43\t * and newly discovered windows are appended, which keeps the terminal presentation stable between refreshes.\n44\t *\n45\t * @private internal utility of `ptbk coder`\n46\t */\n47\texport function mergeHarnessSubscriptionUsage(\n48\t    previousSubscriptionUsage: HarnessSubscriptionUsage | undefined,\n49\t    latestSubscriptionUsage: HarnessSubscriptionUsage,\n50\t): HarnessSubscriptionUsage {\n51\t    if (previousSubscriptionUsage === undefined) {\n52\t        return latestSubscriptionUsage;\n53\t    }\n54\t\n55\t    const latestLimitsByLabel = new Map(\n56\t        latestSubscriptionUsage.limits.map((latestLimit) => [latestLimit.label, latestLimit]),\n57\t    );\n58\t    const previousLimitLabels = new Set(previousSubscriptionUsage.limits.map((previousLimit) => previousLimit.label));\n59\t\n60\t    return {\n61\t        limits: [\n62\t            ...previousSubscriptionUsage.limits.map(\n63\t                (previousLimit) => latestLimitsByLabel.get(previousLimit.label) ?? previousLimit,\n64\t            ),\n65\t            ...latestSubscriptionUsage.limits.filter((latestLimit) => !previousLimitLabels.has(latestLimit.label)),\n66\t        ],\n67\t    };\n68\t}\n69\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"74608ceb-c452-4e82-b385-4ad6b325ff5b","uuid":"3dc21ec4-c239-4247-a88d-d323602064b5","timestamp":"2026-09-17T16:18:29.598Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\ai\\promptbook\\scripts\\run-codex-prompts\\runners\\types\\HarnessSubscriptionUsage.ts","content":"/**\n * One rolling subscription limit reported by a coding harness.\n *\n * @private internal type of `ptbk coder`\n */\nexport type HarnessSubscriptionUsageLimit = {\n    /**\n     * Short, user-facing name of the limit window, for example `5h` or `7d`.\n     */\n    readonly label: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Percentage of this limit which has already been consumed, from 0 through 100.\n     */\n    readonly usedPercentage: number;\n\n    /**\n     * Unix timestamp in seconds at which this limit window resets, when reported by the harness.\n     */\n    readonly resetsAt?: number;\n};\n\n/**\n * Subscription usage snapshot which a coding harness can optionally report.\n *\n * The runner contract deliberately keeps this independent from per-prompt token usage: subscription limits can be\n * shared with other tools and can contain several rolling windows.\n *\n * @private internal type of `ptbk coder`\n */\nexport type HarnessSubscriptionUsage = {\n    /**\n     * Every subscription limit currently reported by the harness, in display order.\n     */\n    readonly limits: ReadonlyArray<HarnessSubscriptionUsageLimit>;\n};\n\n/**\n * Merges a newly reported subset of subscription windows into the latest complete snapshot.\n *\n * Some harnesses emit an update only for the limit whose state changed. Keeping the previous windows means a\n * five-hour update cannot make a still-valid weekly limit disappear from the dashboard. Existing order is preserved\n * and newly discovered windows are appended, which keeps the terminal presentation stable between refreshes.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `ptbk coder`\n */\nexport function mergeHarnessSubscriptionUsage(\n    previousSubscriptionUsage: HarnessSubscriptionUsage | undefined,\n    latestSubscriptionUsage: HarnessSubscriptionUsage,\n): HarnessSubscriptionUsage {\n    if (previousSubscriptionUsage === undefined) {\n        return latestSubscriptionUsage;\n    }\n\n    const latestLimitsByLabel = new Map(\n        latestSubscriptionUsage.limits.map((latestLimit) => [latestLimit.label, latestLimit]),\n    );\n    const previousLimitLabels = new Set(previousSubscriptionUsage.limits.map((previousLimit) => previousLimit.label));\n\n    return {\n        limits: [\n            ...previousSubscriptionUsage.limits.map(\n                (previousLimit) => latestLimitsByLabel.get(previousLimit.label) ?? previousLimit,\n            ),\n            ...latestSubscriptionUsage.limits.filter((latestLimit) => !previousLimitLabels.has(latestLimit.label)),\n        ],\n    };\n}\n","numLines":69,"startLine":1,"totalLines":69}}}

CODEX_JSON_COMPLETION_LINE\n                        : CODEX_COMPLETION_LINE,\n                    idleTimeoutMs: CODEX_COMPLETION_IDLE_MS,\n                    logPath: options.logPath,\n                    shouldPrintLiveOutput: options.shouldPrintLiveOutput,\n                    preserveArtifactsOnSuccess: options.preserveArtifactsOnSuccess,\n                });\n\n                this.rateLimitBackoff.reset();\n                return {\n                    usage: buildCodexUsageFromOutput(output, this.options.model),\n                    loginMethod: parseCodexLoginMethodFromOutput(output),\n                };\n            } catch (error) {\n                const details = extractCodexFailureDetails(error);\n                const failureKind = classifyCodexFailure(details);\n","numLines":80,"startLine":80,"totalLines":218}}}

readString(snapshot.limitName) ?? identifier : undefined;\n\n    return [\n        buildCodexSubscriptionUsageLimit(snapshot.primary, bucketLabel, 'Primary'),\n        buildCodexSubscriptionUsageLimit(snapshot.secondary, bucketLabel, 'Secondary'),\n    ].filter((limit): limit is HarnessSubscriptionUsageLimit => limit !== undefined);\n}\n\n/**\n * Converts one raw Codex rate-limit window to a displayable subscription usage limit.\n *\n * @private helper of `buildCodexSubscriptionUsage`\n */\nfunction buildCodexSubscriptionUsageLimit(\n    rawWindow: unknown,\n    bucketLabel: string | undefined,\n    fallbackWindowLabel: string,\n): HarnessSubscriptionUsageLimit | undefined {\n    if (!isJsonRecord(rawWindow)) {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n\n    const usedPercentage = readPercentage(rawWindow.usedPercent);\n\n    if (usedPercentage === undefined) {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n\n    const windowLabel = formatCodexRateLimitWindowDuration(rawWindow.windowDurationMins) ?? fallbackWindowLabel;\n    const label = bucketLabel ? `${bucketLabel} ${windowLabel}` : windowLabel;\n    const resetsAt = readUnixTimestamp(rawWindow.resetsAt);\n\n    return {\n        label,\n        usedPercentage,\n        ...(resetsAt !== undefined && { resetsAt }),\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Formats the duration of one Codex rolling rate-limit window for compact terminal display.\n *\n * @private helper of `buildCodexSubscriptionUsage`\n */\nfunction formatCodexRateLimitWindowDuration(value: unknown): string | undefined {\n    const durationMinutes = readNonNegativeFiniteNumber(value);\n\n    if (durationMinutes === undefined || durationMinutes === 0) {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n\n    const MINUTES_PER_HOUR = 60;\n    const MINUTES_PER_DAY = 24 * MINUTES_PER_HOUR;\n\n    if (durationMinutes % MINUTES_PER_DAY === 0) {\n        return `${durationMinutes / MINUTES_PER_DAY}d`;\n    }\n\n    if (durationMinutes % MINUTES_PER_HOUR === 0) {\n        return `${durationMinutes / MINUTES_PER_HOUR}h`;\n    }\n\n    return `${durationMinutes}m`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Parses one JSON-RPC line when it is an object.\n *\n * @private helper of `getCodexSubscriptionUsage`\n */\nfunction parseJsonRecord(line: string): JsonRecord | undefined {\n    try {\n        const value = JSON.parse(line) as unknown;\n        return isJsonRecord(value) ? value : undefined;\n    } catch {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Checks whether a value is a JSON object.\n *\n * @private helper of `getCodexSubscriptionUsage`\n */\nfunction isJsonRecord(value: unknown): value is JsonRecord {\n    return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads one non-empty string from an untrusted JSON object.\n *\n * @private helper of `buildCodexSubscriptionUsage`\n */\nfunction readString(value: unknown): string | undefined {\n    return typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() !== '' ? value.trim() : undefined;\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads a finite number which cannot be negative.\n *\n * @private helper of `buildCodexSubscriptionUsage`\n */\nfunction readNonNegativeFiniteNumber(value: unknown): number | undefined {\n    return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 0 ? value : undefined;\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads a valid percentage from the Codex app-server response.\n *\n * @private helper of `buildCodexSubscriptionUsage`\n */\nfunction readPercentage(value: unknown): number | undefined {\n    const percentage = readNonNegativeFiniteNumber(value);\n    return percentage !== undefined && percentage <= 100 ? percentage : undefined;\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads a Unix timestamp in seconds from the Codex app-server response.\n *\n * @private helper of `buildCodexSubscriptionUsage`\n */\nfunction readUnixTimestamp(value: unknown): number | undefined {\n    const timestamp = readNonNegativeFiniteNumber(value);\n    return timestamp !== undefined && timestamp > 0 ? timestamp : undefined;\n}\n","numLines":355,"startLine":1,"totalLines":355}}}

Deeply nested repositories work on Windows too.',\n        sampleCommand: 'ptbk coder run --harness claude-code --isolate',\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Kanban web UI',\n        description:\n            'ptbk coder server keeps running after the queue is empty, watches for new prompt files and serves a Trello-style board where you can edit prompts in the browser.',\n        sampleCommand: 'ptbk coder server --port 4441 --harness claude-code',\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Prompt priorities',\n        description: 'Give prompts a priority and process only the range you want in the current run.',\n        sampleCommand: 'ptbk coder run --harness claude-code --min-priority 1 --max-priority 5',\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Model-specific prompts',\n        description:\n            'Route a prompt to a model family or harness with a backtick token on its [ ] status line, such as [ ] use model `gpt-5.5`. Other runners skip it.',\n        sampleCommand: MODEL_FILTER_COMMAND,\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Agent-specific prompts',\n        description:\n            'Route a prompt to the selected Book with its path, filename, stem or title from the first line, such as [ ] use agent `developer`. Other agents skip it.',\n        sampleCommand: AGENT_FILTER_COMMAND,\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Pacing and retries',\n        description:\n            'Wait a fixed wall-clock duration between prompts. The clock keeps running through a pause and through sleep, and errors retry after a cool-down. The terminal also shows every subscription window a harness reports, with its remaining allowance and reset time. Whenever S is offered it skips whatever the coder waits for right now, down to the harness session limit that would otherwise hold the run for hours.',\n        sampleCommand: 'ptbk coder run --harness claude-code --wait-between-prompts 30m --wait-after-error 10m',\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'List before you run',\n        description:\n            'See every ready, fully authored prompt grouped by priority before starting a harness. Narrow the list by harness, model, agent, or priority range; no files change and no tokens are spent.',\n        sampleCommand: LIST_COMMAND,\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Ping before you queue',\n        description:\n            'ptbk coder ping sends one tiny dummy prompt to a harness and model and reports the answer, the response time and the usage. Use it to check that a harness, model and login work before you queue anything. It also opens the hourly or weekly quota window early, so the quota is already refreshing by the time you need it. If that harness has missing local ignore rules, it asks before adding them to .gitignore.',\n        sampleCommand: PING_COMMAND,\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Keep the 5-hour window rolling',\n        description:\n            'Add --period and the ping repeats until you stop it with CTRL+C. One ping every 5h holds the Claude Code 5-hour limit window open, so a queue you start at any hour already has a refreshing window waiting for it. That costs a handful of tokens per ping instead of a run you have to babysit.',\n        sampleCommand: PING_PERIOD_COMMAND,\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Human in the loop',\n        description:\n            'Confirm each prompt yourself with --no-auto. Press P to pause a running queue, or X to end it after the current prompt. Every press is answered in the Controls panel on the next frame, so you can tell that the key landed even when it changed nothing.',\n        sampleCommand: 'ptbk coder run --harness claude-code --no-auto',\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Nothing to answer',\n        description:\n            'The opposite end: --no-questions never asks anything at all. Installing a missing harness, updating an outdated one or adding ignore rules is skipped and printed as the command which does it manually, so a queue started from a script or a CI job never stops at a prompt nobody is there to answer. ptbk coder init, add, run, ping and server all take it.',\n        sampleCommand: 'ptbk coder run --harness claude-code --no-questions',\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Live status in the prompt file',\n        description:\n            'A [ ] prompt — or plain markdown with no status checkbox — turns into [^] the moment the agent picks it up, and the line names the step that is running. A run started with --agent names that agent in front of its harness, so a finished prompt says which agent implemented it. A prompt without a checkbox starts at priority 0. Use [-] or [.] to keep a task out of the queue, or add <!--ptbk-coder-ignore--> anywhere in a Markdown file to ignore it entirely. It only becomes [x] after the work is implemented, verified and committed. ptbk coder never reverts a [^], so if the queue is killed or crashes you can see which task was left half-done.',\n        sampleCommand: '[^] by Developer on OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` - Implementation in progress',\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Pick up where the run stopped',\n        description:\n            'A dirty working tree stops ptbk coder by default. --git-changes ignore starts anyway, and --git-changes continue resumes the one prompt left in [^] with its half-finished changes still in place. Any harness can take the work over, and the status line then names both the one that started and the one that finished it.',\n        sampleCommand: GIT_CHANGES_CONTINUE_COMMAND,\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Run traces you can read later',\n        description:\n            'Every round leaves a trace in prompts/traces/, named after the prompt file it belongs to. It holds the agent, harness, model, thinking level and login method that ran the prompt, what each step cost and how long it took, and the whole raw output of the harness. The trace is committed together with the prompt, so the run can still be analyzed long after its temporary logs are gone.',\n        sampleCommand: 'prompts/traces/2026-09-0180-add-dark-mode.md',\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Verify and archive',\n        description:\n            'Every successful round writes the agent, harness, model and thinking level into the prompt status line. Walk through completed prompts one by one, archive the finished ones to prompts/done/, and get a repair prompt appended for anything left incomplete. Pick the order with --order from-earliest, from-latest or random.',\n        sampleCommand: VERIFY_COMMAND,\n    },\n    {\n        title: 'Many prompts per file',\n        description:\n            'ptbk coder generate-boilerplates writes one prompt per file by default (--count 5*1). Use --count N*M to pack a whole backlog into fewer files: N files with M prompts each. A --- line separates the sections, every file carries one fresh emoji tag, and each section still runs as its own task.',\n        sampleCommand: GENERATE_BOILERPLATES_COMMAND,\n    },\n];\n","numLines":166,"startLine":1,"totalLines":166}}}

if (idleTimer) {\n                clearTimeout(idleTimer);\n            }\n            idleTimer = setTimeout(finishAfterIdleTimeout, idleTimeoutMs);\n        };\n\n        /**\n         * Processes */\n    public async getSubscriptionUsage(): Promise<HarnessSubscriptionUsage | undefined> {\n        return this.subscriptionUsage;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Runs the prompt using Claude Code and            prompt = buildClaudeCodeSessionResurrectionPrompt(options.prompt, sessionLimit.sessionId);\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            const usage = }\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Waits until the Claude Code session can be resumed, keeping terminal status clear.\n *\n * The wait runs in the `waiting` phase, where the terminal UI offers `S  Skip current Reading it on its own clock instead means the percentages and reset countdowns always\n * describe the present moment, no matter how long the current prompt runs.\n *\n * Refreshes never overlap: a read which is still in flight when the next tick arrives simply skips that tick, so a\n * slow or hanging harness cannot pile up requests. The whole refresh is optional dashboard information, so a harness\n * without subscription limits and a run without a dashboard start no timer at all.\n *\n * @private internal utility of coder run UI\n */\nexport function startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh(options: {\n    readonly runner: PromptRunner;\n    readonly uiState: CoderRunUiState | undefined;\n    readonly refreshIntervalMs?: number;\n}): CoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefreshHandle {\n    const { runner, uiState, refreshIntervalMs = CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS } = options;\n\n    if (!uiState || !runner.getSubscriptionUsage) {\n        return { stop: () => {} };\n    }\n\n    let isRefreshing = false;\n\n    /**\n     * Reads one fresh snapshot unless the previous read has not finished yet.\n     */\n    const refreshSubscriptionUsage = (): void => {\n        if (isRefreshing) {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        isRefreshing = true;\n        void refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage({ runner, uiState }).finally(() => {\n            isRefreshing = false;\n        });\n    };\n\n    // Note: The dashboard shows the usage from its very first frames on instead of waiting out one whole interval\n    refreshSubscriptionUsage();\n\n    const refreshInterval = setInterval(refreshSubscriptionUsage, refreshIntervalMs);\n\n    // Note: Optional dashboard information must never keep the `ptbk coder` process alive after the queue is done\n    refreshInterval.unref?.();\n\n    return {\n        stop(): void {\n            clearInterval(refreshInterval);\n        },\n    };\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":779,"cache_read_input_tokens":157786,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":779},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"74608ceb-c452-4e82-b385-4ad6b325ff5b","uuid":"f1fc4f56-23ef-4ef8-8ad1-623282cfd42f","timestamp":"2026-09-17T16:24:45.234Z","request_id":"req_011Cf9Ke2mwDm8fuNFvDQTgg"}

RunPromptRoundOptions = {\n    options: RunOptions;\n    runner: PromptRunner;\n    runnerMetadata: PromptRunnerMetadata;\n    nextPrompt: PromptSelection;\n    promptLabel: string;\n    resolvedCoderContext?: string;\n    resolvedAgentSystemMessage?: string;\n    isRichUiEnabled: boolean;\n    progressDisplay?: CliProgressDisplay;\n    uiHandle?: CoderRunUiHandle;\n    waitForRequestedPause: WaitForCoderRunPauseCheckpoint;\n\n    /**\n     * Working directory the coding agent, the verification command and the round commit run in.\n     *\n     * Defaults to the nextPrompt,\n    promptLabel,\n    resolvedCoderContext,\n    resolvedAgentSystemMessage,\n    isRichUiEnabled,\n    progressDisplay,\n    uiHandle,\n    waitForRequestedPause,\n    projectPath,\n}: RunPromptRoundOptions): Promise<void> {\n    const roundProjectPath = projectPath ?? process.cwd();\n    const commitMessage = buildCommitMessage(nextPrompt.file, nextPrompt.section);\n    const taskPrompt = buildCodexPrompt(nextPrompt.file, nextPrompt.section);\n    // Prepend agent system message before the task so the harness sees agent instructions first\n    const promptWithAgent = Behavior\n\n                  ${block(increaseHeadings(resolvedAgentSystemMessage))}\n              `,\n          )\n        : taskPrompt;\n    const codexPrompt = appendCoderContext(promptWithAgent, resolvedCoderContext);\n    // Note: Temporary scripts and runtime logs stay in the original project so they outlive an isolated worktree\n    const scriptPath = buildScriptPath(nextPrompt.file, nextPrompt.section);\n    // Note: Read before the first `[^]` rewrite of this round, which would overwrite the report recorded so far\n    const previousRunnerSignatures = resolvePreviousRunnerSignatures(nextPrompt);\n\n    setPromptRoundRunningState({ isRichUiEnabled, promptLabel, scriptPath, uiHandle });\n    await waitForRequestedPause({\n        checkpointLabel: 'preparing the current prompt execution',\n        phase: 'running',\n        statusMessage: 'Preparing prompt execution',\n    });\n\n    const promptExecutionStartedDate = moment();\n    let attemptCount = 1;\n    // Note: The very same snapshot tells which files this round has changed, both for normalizing their line\n    //       endings and for committing only them instead of everything which is changed in the project\n    const roundCommitScope = await captureRoundCommitScopeIfNeeded(options, roundProjectPath);\n\n    await withPromptRuntimeLog(\n        scriptPath,\n        async (logPath) => {\n            let lastError: unknown;\n\n            for (let errorRetryAttempt = 0; errorRetryAttempt <= MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS_AFTER_ERROR; errorRetryAttempt++) {\n                try {\n                    uiHandle?.startCapturingAgentOutput();\n\n                    const result = await runPromptWithTestFeedback({\n                        runner,\n                        prompt: codexPrompt,\n                        scriptPath,\n                        projectPath: roundProjectPath,\n                        promptLabel,\n                        testCommand: options.testCommand,\n                        preserveArtifactsOnSuccess: options.preserveLogs,\n                        logPath,\n                        onAttemptStarted: (nextAttemptCount) => {\n (progress) =>\n                            recordPromptRoundInProgress({\n                                nextPrompt,\n                                runnerMetadata,\n                                previousRunnerSignatures,\n                                thinkingLevel: options.thinkingLevel,\n                                attemptCount,\n                                progress,\n                            }),\n                        waitForPauseCheckpoint: waitForRequestedPause,\n                    });\n\n                    await refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage({\n                        runner,\n                        uiState: uiHandle?.state,\n                    });\n\n                    await finalizeSuccessfulPromptRound({\n                        options,\n                        uiHandle,\n                        waitForRequestedPause,\n                        roundProjectPath,\n                    });\n                    return;\n                } catch (error) {\n                    uiHandle?.stopCapturingAgentOutput();\n                    lastError = error;\n\n                    // Note: A harness which is not logged in answers every retry the same way, so the user gets\n                    //       the sign-in instructions right away instead of after every retry has waited its delay\n                    if (error instanceof AuthenticationError || errorRetryAttempt >= MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS_AFTER_ERROR) {\n                        break;\n                    }\n\n                    await waitAfterErrorBeforeRetry({\n                        options,\n                        error,\n                        attemptedRetries: errorRetryAttempt + 1,\n                        isRichUiEnabled,\n                        progressDisplay,\n                        uiHandle,\n                        waitForRequestedPause,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n\n            await finalizeFailedPromptRound({\n                nextPrompt,\n                runnerMetadata,\n                previousRunnerSignatures,\n                promptExecutionStartedDate,\n                attemptCount,\n                error: lastError,\n                options,\n                logPath,\n                roundCommitScope,\n                uiHandle,\n                waitForRequestedPause,\n                roundProjectPath,\n            });\n\n            throw lastError;\n        },\n        { preserveArtifactsOnSuccess: options.preserveLogs },\n    );\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads the chronological harness report left on the prompt before this round rewrites its in-progress status.\n *\n * Only a prompt resumed through `--git-changes continue` still carries the in-progress `[^]` status when its\n * round starts, so every other round starts a fresh report.\n */\nfunction resolvePreviousRunnerSignatures(nextPrompt: PromptSelection): recordPromptRoundInProgress(options: {\n    nextPrompt: PromptSelection;\n    runnerMetadata: PromptRunnerMetadata;\n    previousRunnerSignatures?: PromptRunnerAttribution;\n    thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel;\n    attemptCount: number;\n    progress: CoderRunStepProgress;\n}): Promise<void> {\n    const { nextPrompt, runnerMetadata, previousRunnerSignatures, thinkingLevel, attemptCount, progress.startedStepKind,\n        ...runnerMetadata,\n        previousRunnerSignatures,\n        attemptCount,\n        loginMethod: progress.loginMethod,\n        thinkingLevel,\n    });\n    // writePromptFile(nextPrompt.file);\n}\n\n/**\n * Sleeps `options.waitAfterError` while keeping the rich UI and plain console in sync, then resets state for the retry.\n */\nasync function waitAfterErrorBeforeRetry(options: {\n    options: RunOptions;\n    error: unknown;\n    attemptedRetries: number;\n    isRichUiEnabled: boolean;\n    progressDisplay?: CliProgressDisplay;\n    uiHandle?: CoderRunUiHandle;\n    waitForRequestedPause: WaitForCoderRunPauseCheckpoint;\n}): Promise<void> {\n    const {\n        options: runOptions,\n        error,\n        attemptedRetries,\n   `Prompt round failed (retry ${attemptedRetries}/${MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS_AFTER_ERROR}): ${errorMessage}`,\n            ),\n        );\n    }\n\n    const retryDeadlineTimeMs = Date.now() + runOptions.waitAfterError;\n\n    await waitForRequestedPause({\n        checkpointLabel: 'waiting after error before retrying the prompt',\n        phase: 'waiting',\n        statusMessage: `Waiting before retry ${attemptedRetries}/${MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS_AFTER_ERROR} after error`,\n    });\n\n    progressDisplay?.pauseTimer();\n    uiHandle?.state.pauseTimer();\n\n    await sleepWithCountdown({\n progressDisplay?.resumeTimer();\n    uiHandle?.state.resumeTimer();\n    uiHandle?.state.setPhase('running');\n    uiHandle?.state.setStatusMessage(`Retrying prompt (retry setPromptRoundRunningState(options: {\n    isRichUiEnabled: boolean;\n    promptLabel: string;\n    scriptPath: string;\n    uiHandle?: CoderRunUiHandle;\n}): void {\n    const { isRichUiEnabled,   uiHandle?.state.setStatusMessage('Running');\n\n    if (isRichUiEnabled) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    console.info(colors.blue(`Processing ${promptLabel}`));\n}\n\n/**\n * Finalizes a successful runnerMetadata: PromptRunnerMetadata;\n    previousRunnerSignatures?: PromptRunnerAttribution;\n    promptExecutionStartedDate: moment.Moment;\n    result: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof runPromptWithTestFeedback>>;\n    commitMessage: string;\n    logPath: string;\n    roundCommitScope?: CoderCommitScope;\n    isRichUiEnabled: boolean;\n    progressDisplay?: CliProgressDisplay;\n    uiHandle?: CoderRunUiHandle;\n    waitForRequestedPause: WaitForCoderRunPauseCheckpoint;\n    roundProjectPath: string;\n}): Promise<void> {\n    const {\n        options: runOptions,\n        nextPrompt,\n        runnerMetadata,\n        previousRunnerSignatures,\n        promptExecutionStartedDate,\n        result,\n        commitMessage,\n        logPath,\n        roundCommitScope,\n        isRichUiEnabled,\n        progressDisplay,\n        uiHandle,\n        waitForRequestedPause,\n        roundProjectPath,\n    } = options;\n\n    uiHandle?.stopCapturingAgentOutput();\n    await waitForRequestedPause({\n        checkpointLabel: 'recording the successful prompt result',\n        phase: 'running',\n        statusMessage: 'Recording prompt result',\n    });\n\n    markPromptDone({\n        file: nextPrompt.file,\n        section: nextPrompt.section,\n        steps: result.steps,\n        ...runnerMetadata,\n        previousRunnerSignatures,\n        attemptCount: result.attemptCount,\n        loginMethod: result.loginMethod,\n        thinkingLevel: runOptions.thinkingLevel,\n    });\n    // Note: The prompt status is always written into the original project, an isolated round transports\n    //       its own changes back through the merge instead\n    await writePromptFile(nextPrompt.file);\n    // Note: Written before the round is committed, so the trace of the round lands in the very same commit\n    //       as the prompt it describes, and before the live runtime log it is built from is deleted\n    await recordPromptRoundTrace({\n        options: runOptions,\n        nextPrompt,\n        runnerMetadata,\n        promptExecutionStartedDate,\n        attemptCount: result.attemptCount,\n        logPath,\n        outcome: { kind: 'succeeded', steps: result.steps, loginMethod: result.loginMethod },\n    });\n    await normalizeLineEndingsForCurrentRound(runOptions, roundProjectPath, roundCommitScope);\n    await recordPromptDurationInEstimateCache({\n        options: runOptions,\n        runnerMetadata,\n        promptExecutionStartedDate,\n    });\n\n    if (!runOptions.noCommit) {\n        await waitForCommitConfirmationIfNeeded({\n            options: runOptions,\n            commitMessage,\n            isRichUiEnabled,\n            progressDisplay,\n 'Committing changes',\n        });\n        await commitChanges(commitMessage, {\n            autoPush: runOptions.autoPush,\n            // Note: Only the prompt file and the files the coding agent has changed belong to this round,\n            //       everything which was already changed before the round started stays in the working tree\n            relevantPaths: roundCommitScope && (await resolveCoderCommitScopePaths(roundCommitScope)),\n            // Keep the live runtime log out of default commits because it is deleted after a successful round.\n            excludePaths: runOptions.preserveLogs ? undefined : [logPath],\n            projectPath: roundProjectPath,\n            // Note: An isolated round commits only the agent changes, so a task that needed none must not fail here\n            isEmptyCommitAllowed: runOptions.isIsolated,\n        });\n    } else {\n        uiHandle?.state.setStatusMessage('Leaving changes uncommitted');\n    }\n\n    if file: nextPrompt.file,\n        section: nextPrompt.section,\n        ...runnerMetadata,\n        thinkingLevel: runOptions.thinkingLevel,\n        testCommand: runOptions.testCommand,\n        attemptCount,\n        startedDate: promptExecutionStartedDate,\n        finishedDate: moment(),\n        outcome,\n        logPath,\n    });\n}\n\n/**\n * Waits for the optional user confirmation {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cf9Kgdurt5opfiVGUNSov","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01An71Uk2oLsQYzVWp2XQJmV","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\ai\\promptbook\\scripts\\run-codex-prompts\\ui\\startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh.test.ts","content":"import moment from 'moment';\nimport type { PromptRunner } from '../runners/types/PromptRunner';\nimport { CoderRunUiState } from './CoderRunUiState';\nimport {\n    CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS,\n    startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh,\n} from './startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh';\n\n/**\n * Creates the smallest runner shape needed for periodic subscription-usage tests.\n */\nfunction createRunner(getSubscriptionUsage?: PromptRunner['getSubscriptionUsage']): PromptRunner {\n    return {\n        name: 'test-harness',\n        runPrompt: jest.fn(),\n        getSubscriptionUsage,\n    };\n}\n\ndescribe('startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh', () => {\n    beforeEach(() => {\n        jest.useFakeTimers();\n    });\n\n    afterEach(() => {\n        jest.useRealTimers();\n    });\n\n    it('refreshes the usage percentages every 5 seconds without waiting for the current prompt', async () => {\n        const uiState = new CoderRunUiState(moment());\n        let usedPercentage = 10;\n        const getSubscriptionUsage = jest.fn(async () => ({\n            limits: [{ label: '5h', usedPercentage: (usedPercentage += 10) }],\n        }));\n\n        const refreshHandle = startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh({\n            runner: createRunner(getSubscriptionUsage),\n            uiState,\n        });\n\n        // Note: The very first read happens right away, so the dashboard never starts with an empty usage row\n        await jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);\n        expect(uiState.subscriptionUsage).toEqual({ limits: [{ label: '5h', usedPercentage: 20 }] });\n\n        await jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS);\n        expect(uiState.subscriptionUsage).toEqual({ limits: [{ label: '5h', usedPercentage: 30 }] });\n\n        await jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS);\n        expect(uiState.subscriptionUsage).toEqual({ limits: [{ label: '5h', usedPercentage: 40 }] });\n\n        refreshHandle.stop();\n    });\n\n    it('refreshes nothing after the run has stopped it', async () => {\n        const uiState = new CoderRunUiState(moment());\n        const getSubscriptionUsage = jest.fn(async () => ({ limits: [{ label: '5h', usedPercentage: 12 }] }));\n\n        const refreshHandle = startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh({\n            runner: createRunner(getSubscriptionUsage),\n            uiState,\n        });\n\n        await jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0);\n        refreshHandle.stop();\n        await jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(10 * CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS);\n\n        expect(getSubscriptionUsage).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);\n    });\n\n    it('skips a tick while the previous read of a slow harness is still in flight', async () => {\n        const uiState = new CoderRunUiState(moment());\n        let resolveSubscriptionUsage: (() => void) | undefined;\n        const getSubscriptionUsage = jest.fn(\n            async () =>\n                await new Promise<undefined>((resolve) => {\n                    resolveSubscriptionUsage = () => resolve(undefined);\n                }),\n        );\n\n        const refreshHandle = startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh({\n            runner: createRunner(getSubscriptionUsage),\n            uiState,\n        });\n\n        await jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(3 * CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS);\n        expect(getSubscriptionUsage).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);\n\n        resolveSubscriptionUsage?.();\n        await jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS);\n        expect(getSubscriptionUsage).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);\n\n        refreshHandle.stop();\n    });\n\n    it('starts no timer for a harness which cannot report subscription usage', async () => {\n        const uiState = new CoderRunUiState(moment());\n\n        const refreshHandle = startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh({\n            runner: createRunner(),\n            uiState,\n        });\n\n        await jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(10 * CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS);\n\n        expect(jest.getTimerCount()).toBe(0);\n        expect(uiState.subscriptionUsage).toBeUndefined();\n        refreshHandle.stop();\n    });\n\n    it('starts no timer for a run without a dashboard', async () => {\n        const getSubscriptionUsage = jest.fn(async () => ({ limits: [{ label: '5h', usedPercentage: 12 }] }));\n\n        const refreshHandle = startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh({\n            runner: createRunner(getSubscriptionUsage),\n            uiState: undefined,\n        });\n\n        await jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(10 * CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS);\n\n        expect(jest.getTimerCount()).toBe(0);\n        expect(getSubscriptionUsage).not.toHaveBeenCalled();\n        refreshHandle.stop();\n    });\n});\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":344,"cache_read_input_tokens":162622,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":344},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"74608ceb-c452-4e82-b385-4ad6b325ff5b","uuid":"7088a5b6-dbf0-4fb1-a659-9377538b1346","timestamp":"2026-09-17T16:25:25.388Z","request_id":"req_011Cf9KgdToz8JP3UpbjY8jh"}
