Admins can now run and stop projects directly from `/admin/projects`.\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server `/superadmin/environment` editor so super admins can add arbitrary valid `.env` variables directly from the UI. Every variable already persisted in the VPS `.env` file is now listed automatically — including integrations such as `ELEVEN_LABS_API_KEY` — while sensitive values remain masked and the server-side super-admin-only write policy remains enforced.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server home page so the temporary federated-agents loading section is not shown before federation data is available. When no federated servers or agents are returned, the homepage now remains free of that section instead of briefly showing it.\n-   Fixed cross-platform unit-test portability: macOS canonical temporary paths no longer conflict with test assertions or Git exclusions, shell-script links normalize Windows-style separators on every host, document-scraper unit tests no longer require locally installed Pandoc or LibreOffice, import repair handles Windows paths when run on another platform, and Agents Server builds clear stale Next route types left by another build output directory.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server home page so the temporary federated-agents loading section is not shown before federation data is available. When no federated servers or agents are returned, the homepage now remains free of that section instead of briefly showing it.\n\n-   Unified Agents Server DNS setup guidance. `/superadmin/servers` and `/admin/email-server` now reuse one record-instruction panel with consistent record columns, setup steps, conflict guidance, and DNS-provider documentation links; server-domain diagnostics still offer one compatible A/AAAA/CNAME alternative, while email setup correctly requires every MX/SPF/DMARC/TLS record shown.\n\n-   Improved Agents Server `/admin/users` with a practical admin table that puts named users first and clearly groups anonymous visitor accounts below them. User creation now opens a create-server-style dialog with a browser Web Crypto secure password generator, and every user links to a detail page with recent chat activity plus direct links to filtered Chat history and Task manager views. Chat history now supports preserving a user filter through table, thread, and CSV views, and task/chat tables link back to the relevant user.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server initial chat greeting so a partially loaded agent never shows its opaque permanent id. The canonical chat now reuses the already resolved human-readable agent title until the remote agent profile is available.\n\n-   Fixed the default Coder project npm scripts to use the locally installed `ptbk` command expected by the Coder boilerplate verification.\n\n-   Enhanced Agents Server admin page tabs with one shared underline-style navigation component. Configuration, storage, and task-manager scope tabs now use consistent spacing, active-state styling, hover states, and accessible current-page semantics.\n\n-   Unified the Agents Server per-server and VPS-wide task managers. The VPS-wide `/superadmin/task-manager` now shows the same task details, target links, log controls, task detail links, cancellation/retry actions, terminal button, and bulk cancellation action as `/admin/task-manager`, with only the owning **Server** column added; cross-server actions preserve each server's isolated context, and the former `/admin/task-manager-vps` URL redirects to the new super-admin route.\n\n-   Scoped agent project reporting correctly across standalone VPS servers. The per-server `/admin/projects` dashboard remains limited to agents owned by the current server, while the super-admin `/superadmin/resource-monitor` project storage panel now aggregates every registered server and labels each project with its owning server. Project and agent links stay local for the current server and use the owning server's absolute URL for foreign projects, so a VPS-wide report cannot open another server's project under the wrong database namespace.\n\n-   Simplified the Agents Server homepage to keep only the **List** agents view. Removed the Graph, Office, Maze, and Pixel view switcher/renderers, their unused layout/state/test/CSS code, the Pixel Agents asset route, and the now-unused `reactflow` and `pixel-agents` dependencies; the existing list and federated-agent cards remain available.\n\n-   Added **VPS server setup** tasks to the Agents Server `/admin/task-manager`. Creating a new server and the automatic Let's Encrypt certificate obtain/renew maintenance now persist their full task lifecycle, including start, finish, duration, worker, queue, attempt, error, and searchable target details, and the task's **Open** link leads to the super admin `/superadmin/servers` page.\n\n-   Added project DNS setup instructions to the Agents Server `/admin/servers` project-domain panel. Administrators can now choose between configuring one project-specific hostname or a wildcard for all generated project domains, and between an A record pointing to the VPS or a CNAME pointing to the server domain.\n\n-   Fixed the standalone VPS self-update **Total** time in the Agents Server `/admin/task-manager` so it reports the real update duration instead of `0s`. A successful self-update restarts the server, which usually terminates the detached installer before it can record its own `FINISHED_AT`; the persisted job snapshot now falls back to the status file's last-write time for such stale runs, and the task-manager row no longer collapses an unknown finish time to the start time (showing `-` instead of a fabricated zero-second total).\n\n-   Linked every Agents Server `/admin/task-manager` task to the page it operates on, and back, as one universal pattern. Each background task now shows an **Open** button that jumps to what it is doing: a **chat completion** or **chat timeout** task opens its chat thread (`/agents/<agent>/chat?chat=<chatId>`), a **VPS self-update** task opens the `/superadmin/update` panel, and a **browser preview** task opens the previewed page in a new tab. The forward link is resolved through a single shared `resolveAdminChatTaskTargetLink` helper reused by both the task-manager table row and the per-task detail page (`/admin/task-manager/<taskId>`), which already shows only that one task. The reverse direction is now complete too: the self-update panel links to its own task in the task manager, and the existing per-message **Task** link on `/admin/chat-history` (chat → task) now reuses the same shared `buildAdminChatTaskDetailHref` builder, so both link directions stay consistent (DRY).\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server so administrator and super-admin **System warnings** are never shown to — nor delivered to — regular or anonymous visitors. These warnings (server **resource pressure**, a **misconfigured Shibboleth login method**, and **missing core agents**) describe problems only the responsible administrator should act on, but the misconfigured-Shibboleth warning previously decorated the top-level **System** menu with a warning triangle even for signed-out visitors, and the raw Shibboleth activation/configuration status was serialized into every page. Each System warning is now gated behind the matching admin capability through a single shared `resolveHeaderSystemWarnings` policy reused by both the top-level System label indicator and the individual System submenu entries, so the three indicators can no longer disagree or leak. The Shibboleth menu status is now resolved server-side only for administrators (non-admin viewers receive an inert `SHIBBOLETH_AUTHENTICATION_MENU_STATUS_HIDDEN` status), matching how the resource-monitor and core-agents warnings were already withheld from the client, so the warning information is no longer available client-side for viewers who may not see it. Finally, the whole **System** menu — like the **Documentation** menu — is now hidden entirely from visitors who are not signed in, so anonymous visitors no longer see a System entry at all. The separate `/api/auth/shibboleth/status` login endpoint that the login dialog uses to offer the Shibboleth sign-in button is intentionally left unchanged.\n\n-   Added a self-contained **Stalwart Mail Server** to standalone VPS Agents Server installations. Stalwart is installed, bootstrapped with local storage and automatic DKIM keys, started as a system service, and connected to each server through an authenticated DATA-stage MTA hook and local SMTP submission account. Every active agent now receives normalized dotted, compact, permanent-id, and plus-tagged addresses on the server domain; incoming mail creates a dedicated durable chat with an `EMAIL` source flag and a normalized passwordless ad-hoc sender, while the completed agent answer is sent with the agent’s display name, from the exact alias originally addressed, and to all original To/Cc/From participants. Unknown local recipients receive the required apology plus the server’s public-agent directory. Per-server `/admin/email-server` and VPS-wide `/superadmin/email-server` pages expose health, synchronization, aliases, and complete MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC/TLS-RPT/MTA-STS/CAA/PTR guidance, and agent profile/context-menu/QR surfaces now use the same shared address formatter. A backwards-compatible migration extends durable and audit chat-history sources with `EMAIL`, and the VPS installer provisions a normal Stalwart application administrator, removes the temporary recovery credential, provisions transport secrets, and opens only public inbound SMTP port 25 while keeping submission and management local.\n\n-   Added ex-post reinstatement of the bundled Agents Server agents so an admin can restore the default and core agents without recreating the server. There are two kinds of bundled agents: the **normal default agents** (in `agents/default/`) that showcase what Promptbook agents can do, and the **core agents** (in `agents/default/.core/`, such as Adam, Expert, Creator, and Teacher) that are used as the shared base every other agent inherits from. When any of these are missing, admins now see an admin-only notice on the home page — a **warning** for missing core agents and an **information** banner for missing normal default agents — each with a single button that recreates only the missing agents while leaving every existing (possibly edited) agent untouched. The reinstatement reuses the exact same creation logic that runs when a server is first created (a shared \"create only the missing agents\" helper is now used by both the core-agent seeder and the new default-agent reinstatement). A new admin **Core Agents** page (`/admin/core-agents`, in System → Administration) tracks whether every core agent is present, explains why each core agent exists, links to each present agent's editable book, and shows — for reference only, never as a warning — whether a present core agent differs from the bundled repository version. Missing core agents also raise a warning indicator on the System menu's Administration category. The whole flow is available only to per-server admins (not regular users) and is backed by a new admin-gated `/api/admin/default-agents/reinstate` endpoint.\n\n-   Moved every Agents Server **Super Admin** page from `/admin/*` to a dedicated `/superadmin/*` route root, so the VPS-wide superadmin area is separated from the per-server `/admin/*` administration pages. The nine relocated pages are **Servers** (`/superadmin/servers`), **Environment variables** (`/superadmin/environment`), **Resource monitor** (`/superadmin/resource-monitor`), **Update** (`/superadmin/update`), **Database** (`/superadmin/database`), **Internal S3** (`/superadmin/internal-s3`), **Logs** (`/superadmin/logs`), **Harness auth** (`/superadmin/harness-auth`), and **CLI access** (`/superadmin/cli-access`); each page directory keeps its own components, server actions, and helpers and moves wholesale. The System menu links, the raw-IP first-run `?setup=1` redirect, the post-delete server redirect, the file-upload-unavailable notice link, the shared **Server configuration** and **Storage** tab shells (whose remaining Metadata/Limits/Files tabs stay under `/admin/*`), and every affected `revalidatePath` call now point at the new `/superadmin/*` routes, and `superadmin` is registered as a reserved top-level path so it is never mistaken for an agent name. The backing HTTP APIs are intentionally left at `/api/admin/*` — only the browser-facing page routes changed — and the per-server administration pages (models, metadata, limits, users, files, projects, task manager, chat history, and the rest) stay under `/admin/*`.\n\n-   Fixed the standalone VPS Agents Server so chat completion tasks now run for **every** server on the VPS, not only the first one. On a VPS hosting several servers (for example `lts.example.com`, `lts1.example.com`, and `lts2.example.com`), messages sent to agents on any server other than the first previously stayed pending forever because the background durable-chat worker only ever advanced jobs for the default server: its loopback self-call has no server `host` header, so server routing resolved to the single default table prefix and every other server's queued and running jobs were never claimed or synchronized. The worker's coordinator poll now fans out across **all** registered servers each tick — running expired-job recovery and the local runner inside each server's own routing context via a shared server-context override (an immediate per-message trigger still stays scoped to its own server) — so answers are produced and completed for every server, and one failing server never blocks the others. Added a companion **VPS-wide task manager** (superadmin only, `/admin/task-manager-vps`, linked from the System menu) that aggregates the durable background tasks of every server on the VPS into one read-only table with a **Server** column, reusing the existing per-server task-manager UI and the shared injected-task pipeline; the two task managers are interlinked with **This server** / **All servers (VPS)** tabs shown to superadmins.\n\n-   Fixed the OpenAI Codex sign-in on the Agents Server `/admin/harness-auth` page so admins can actually authenticate the ChatGPT subscription instead of paying per token. The interactive authentication terminal previously launched the bare `codex` CLI, which starts the Codex chat TUI (not a login) and immediately dies in the non-interactive browser terminal with `Session terminated, killing shell...`; the installer now runs `codex login --device-auth`, whose device-code flow needs no local browser callback and works from the embedded terminal. The Harness Auth page now shows a guided OpenAI Codex wizard that explains the difference between the **ChatGPT subscription** (uses the signed-in ChatGPT account quota, no per-token OpenAI API charges) and the **OpenAI API key** (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, billed per token), walks a first-time admin through the device sign-in step by step, and shows which method is currently in use — resolved server-side by reusing the same `Logged in using ChatGPT` detection (now a shared `CODEX_CHATGPT_LOGIN_STATUS_NEEDLE` constant reused by the Codex runner script) that the runtime uses to pick between the ChatGPT account and `OPENAI_API_KEY`.\n\n-   Made Agents Server agent IDs case-insensitive so the same permanent agent id resolves to the same agent regardless of the letter casing used in the URL. For example `/agents/doQMRg82izNfJa/chat`, `/agents/doqmrg82iznfja/chat`, and `/agents/DOQMRG82IZNFJA/chat` now all open the same agent and redirect to its canonical id. Human-readable agent-name lookups stay exact, while permanent-id lookups now match case-insensitively through a single shared `buildAgentNameOrPermanentIdFilter` helper (Supabase/PostgREST `ilike` with `LIKE` wildcards escaped) that the core `AgentCollectionInSupabase` and every Agents Server agent lookup reuse, plus a shared `isSameAgentPermanentId` comparison used by the in-memory route, ownership, and custom-domain resolvers. For example `/agents/doQMRg82izNfJa/chat`, `/agents/doqmrg82iznfja/chat`, and `/agents/DOQMRG82IZNFJA/chat` now all open the same agent and redirect to its canonical id. Human-readable agent-name lookups stay exact, while permanent-id lookups now match case-insensitively through a single shared `buildAgentNameOrPermanentIdFilter` helper (Supabase/PostgREST `ilike` with `LIKE` wildcards escaped) that the core `AgentCollectionInSupabase` and every Agents Server agent lookup reuse, plus a shared `isSameAgentPermanentId` comparison used by the in-memory route, ownership, and custom-domain resolvers.\n\n-   Made the standalone VPS Agents Server manage its Let's Encrypt certificates automatically for every assigned domain, whether the domain belongs to the server or to a project. A new process-wide certificate scheduler periodically runs a lightweight `install.sh apply-certificates` maintenance pass that reuses the existing idempotent per-domain certificate configuration: it obtains a certificate for any domain that still lacks one and renews any certificate close to expiry, then re-renders nginx so freshly issued certificates start serving HTTPS. This means a server created **before** its DNS is configured now gets its certificate on its own once the DNS starts resolving — no manual `apply-domains` rerun needed — and expiring certificates are renewed without intervention. The maintenance pass never restarts the Agents Server, never touches the firewall, and keeps every domain isolated in its own certificate lineage, so a single domain failing to validate (or a project failing to run) can never take the main server domain offline; the raw-IP default server and plain-HTTP fallback keep the server reachable from the web throughout. The failed-issuance warning now points operators at the automatic retry (and the immediate `install.sh apply-certificates` command).\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server `/admin/task-manager` **All** history view so tasks are ordered by finished time, with the newest finished task on top. The `All` view previously ordered rows by last-update time, which let a self-update that finished long ago sit above chat completions that finished more recently. The default `All` ordering now reuses the shared task timeline timestamp (which resolves to `finishedAt` for terminal tasks) in both the SQLite comparator and the PostgreSQL `ORDER BY`, while still-active tasks keep their start/queue placement instead of dropping to the bottom.\n\n-   Moved the standalone VPS Agents Server installer from `other/vps/install.sh` to `install.sh` in the repository root so the entry-point script is easy to find, while its dependency scripts (for example `other/vps/test-nginx-config-generation.sh`) stay under `other/vps/` and are called relative to the root installer. The self-update flow, the installer self-references it persists into `PTBK_VPS_INSTALL_SCRIPT`, the Agents Server installer-path resolver, and the documented `curl … | bash` deploy instructions now point at the root `install.sh`; the resolver still falls back across candidate paths, so servers self-updating from an older release keep working across the move.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat feedback stars so unpicked stars no longer stay yellow. The shared chat feedback controls now render CSS-colored star icons with their resolved color, fill, and stroke state applied through shared CSS variables and inline SVG icon styles instead of the native colored emoji glyph, inactive stars are hollow even when generic SVG styles are present, and the compact response control plus rating modal share the same rating-message key resolution so both reflect the picked rating consistently.\n\n-   Added `--env` to the standalone VPS Agents Server installer. Fresh installs now default to the `preview` environment, while `--env live`, `--env production`, and `--env lts` select the corresponding Promptbook branch and persist it as `PROMPTBOOK_REPOSITORY_REF`.\n\n-   Fixed the standalone VPS Agents Server installer so `curl ... | bash -s -- ...` works under `set -u`. Bash leaves `BASH_SOURCE` empty when executing a script from stdin, so the installer entrypoint now uses a dedicated sourced-script detector and the self-update script-copy step skips the stable-copy rerun when the running installer has no readable file path. The root verification setup now also resolves the same local Agents Server aliases, keeps the CLI build-command unit test mocked at the direct helper import paths, and raises the shared Agents Server production build heap limit after verification exposed a 4 GiB Next build OOM.\n\n-   Fixed standalone VPS Agents Server multi-server isolation so servers hosted on one VPS can no longer leak agents, projects, metadata, users, chats, or any other server-scoped data into each other. Each registered server now has **its own SQLite database file** (`servers/<server-namespace>.sqlite` next to the existing database), and one **VPS-wide SQLite registry database** (the existing `agents-server.sqlite`) owned by the super-admin holds only the `_Server` list of servers. The SQLite Supabase-shaped adapter routes every table access through a single choke point — VPS-level `_`-prefixed tables go to the registry database while server-prefixed tables go to the owning server's database under clean unprefixed names — so all existing data access code works unchanged. `/admin/servers` create/rename/delete now manages persistent registry rows with stable ids (renaming a domain keeps the server's data; deleting a registration keeps its database file on disk), the `SERVERS` environment variable remains only a projection for nginx/certbot provisioning and Edge middleware host matching, and creating a server no longer overwrites the shared `SUPABASE_TABLE_PREFIX` (the root cause of servers flipping into one another's tables). Domains listed in `SERVERS` are auto-registered into the registry on first boot, so a freshly installed VPS bootstraps itself, and the embedded database admin now targets the current server's isolated database only.\n\n-   Added a **Cancel all active tasks** action to the Agents Server `/admin/task-manager`. A guarded button in the background-tasks header requests cancellation of every active (queued + running) durable chat task across all users in one confirmed, reason-required step via a new `/api/admin/chat-tasks/cancel-all` endpoint, reusing the existing single-task cancellation flow for each task and reporting how many tasks were matched and cancelled.\n\n-   Separated the Agents Server `/admin/chat-history` by chat thread instead of one mixed pile. A new **Chat thread** filter (grouped from `chatId` by a new `/api/chat-history/threads` endpoint) narrows the table view to a single conversation once an agent is picked, and the CSV export honors it. The chat transcript view now lists recorded threads and opens one conversation at a time (never mixing threads) and always renders in bubble mode regardless of the article-mode control-panel preference. The table message column now renders Markdown, and links into chat history (super-admin external-chat banner and admin conversation search results) now deep-link to the most detailed view — the recorded conversation in chat view — when the agent and thread are known.\n\n-   Added sortable column headers to Agents Server administration tables, with shared sorting controls and helpers reused across task manager, chat history, chat feedback, messages, files, images, API tokens, metadata, servers, environment variables, usage detail, Shibboleth, and resource monitor tables. Paginated admin lists now send whitelisted sort fields to their loaders so the full result set is ordered before pagination.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server manGo new-agent wizard desktop rail so the left panel scrolls independently on short viewports, keeping the stepper and progress controls reachable while preserving the existing fullscreen layout.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server manGo new-agent wizard so the right content panel scrolls independently inside the fullscreen layout, keeping long Book, knowledge, and test steps reachable without moving the desktop rail.\n\n-   Added a classic Book editor exit from the Agents Server manGo new-agent wizard. A small Book button in the manGo rail now opens the existing classic editor with the current partially created draft, including the generated book text and ready knowledge sources, so users can finish creation outside the manGo flow.\n\n-   Added **Download .book** to the Agents Server agent context menu. The action downloads the stored source book for the selected authenticated local agent using the same safe filename sanitization as book ZIP exports, while the existing inherited-source `/api/book` route remains unchanged.\n\n-   Improved Agents Server chat source chips so JSON-like and binary image citations no longer show raw payload text. Source labels now fall back to compact URL snippets when a source URL is known, or type labels such as `JSON file` and `JPEG image` when it is not; source chips now use semantic SVG icons for websites, JSON, documents, media, archives, and related file types, with URL-backed image citations rendered as thumbnails.\n\n-   Extended runnable Agents Server agent projects with durable public runtime exposure. Project pages and the internal agent-project runtime API can now start dev or static project runtimes, the server persists assigned ports and project subdomains, production Linux runtimes are started as dedicated pm2 processes, and the standalone VPS installer reads the managed project-domain list to configure nginx reverse proxying and SSL certificates. `/admin/servers` now shows project subdomains assigned below each server domain.\n\n-   Fixed standalone VPS Agents Server self-updates so newly required host software is installed through the same shared dependency path as fresh installs. The code-server installer now uses the standalone release installer instead of global npm installation, avoiding the `Please pass --unsafe-perm to npm to install code-server` failure during `/admin/update`.\n\n-   Added super-admin browser VS Code access for Agents Server agent projects. Project pages now show an **Open VS Code** action and support the GitHub-style `.` shortcut for super admins, launching a per-project `code-server` session rooted at the project directory with matching light/dark theme settings, editable files, git tooling, and terminal CWD on the project root. Standalone VPS installs now install `code-server`, proxy VS Code sessions through an authenticated nginx subpath, route `install.sh` on already installed servers into self-update, and share dependency installation between fresh installs and self-updates so new server-side software dependencies are applied during updates.\n\n-   Added runnable local agent projects to the Agents Server. Local agents can now ask the server for a tracked free port, start a server-owned project dev command, or start a static file server for plain project folders; the prompt instructions expose the internal runtime API through environment variables instead of embedding secrets. Project runtime ports now appear in `/admin/resource-monitor` with links to the live port and owning project plus terminate/release controls, and each project page shows whether its project is running or has an assigned port with the same terminate/release action.\n\n-   Fixed the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal avatar preview so the sample now renders the existing shared `AsciiOctopus` canvas avatar directly, matching the web avatar visual instead of the blocky terminal rasterization.\n\n-   Fixed the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal avatar alignment so the web sample now centers the shared animated `AsciiOctopus` lines to the same dashboard width as the surrounding live-terminal boxes.\n\n-   Added persistent per-agent browser profiles to the Agents Server. Every agent now browses in its own isolated Playwright profile (persistent Chromium user-data directory), so cookies, session tokens, logged-in sessions, and other browser data survive across chats and server restarts — for example an agent signed into a social network stays signed in without the user logging in again. The `run_browser` tool resolves the acting agent from the hidden tool runtime context, and the live browser preview (opened from knowledge/citation chips in chat) now runs on the same agent profile via a new `agent` query parameter of `/api/page-preview/stream` threaded through a new optional `agentIdentifier` prop of `<Chat/>`, so when the user logs in somewhere inside the live session the login is saved into the agent's profile for future agent browsing. The profile is managed through the wallet: a new agent-scoped `BROWSER_PROFILE` wallet record type (added by a backwards-compatible migration) stores only the link to the profile directory on the filesystem (default under `.promptbook/agents-server/browser/profiles`, overridable via `AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE_STORAGE_DIRECTORY`), it is registered automatically on first agent browsing and editable at `/system/user-wallet`. `BrowserConnectionProvider` now caches one browser context per profile directory and closes contexts with no open pages after an idle timeout (`RUN_BROWSER_CONTEXT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 10 minutes) — the browser is not kept alive while unused, only the profile data stays permanent. The wallet UI and menu are now labeled **Agent Wallet** (records belong to agents, each agent has its own wallet; the `/system/user-wallet` route is kept for backwards compatibility).\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server live browser preview (shown when a cited page cannot be embedded as an iframe) into a remote-desktop-like session inspired by Chrome Remote Desktop and AnyDesk. The preview now forwards natural browser interactions to the server-side headless browser — hovering, clicking, double-clicking (click counts are tracked client-side like in remote desktop viewers), dragging and text selection via raw pointer presses and releases, mouse-wheel scrolling, and full keyboard typing including shortcuts (keys outside the US layout fall back to text insertion). A browser-like toolbar adds back/forward/reload, an editable address bar (submitted URLs are SSRF-checked server-side), local zoom (Ctrl+wheel, pinch, or toolbar buttons, 50–300 %), an \"Open in new tab\" link, and a full screen mode. The remote viewport is sized dynamically: it follows the measured preview area and full screen changes instead of the previous fixed 1280x800. Stream frames are now sourced from a CDP `Page.startScreencast` — pushed on every repaint for smooth video playback and scrolling, idle-cheap, capped at ~15 fps, with a heartbeat that re-sends the last frame so proxies do not drop quiet streams — while the previous screenshot-polling loop remains as a fallback. The input protocol (`src/book-components/Chat/Chat/pagePreview/`) is shared between the new `<LiveBrowserPreview/>` component and the `/api/page-preview/input` route, events are delivered strictly in order with move/wheel coalescing, a new `/api/page-preview/state` route keeps the toolbar in sync with navigations happening inside the page, and a reconnect overlay appears when the stream drops.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder` artificial waits so they are tied to wall-clock deadlines instead of decrementing only while the Node process is actively awake. `--wait-between-prompts`, `--wait-after-prompt`, `--wait-after-error`, OpenAI Codex rate-limit backoff, and Claude Code session-limit resurrection waits now elapse during `p`/web-UI pauses and while the computer sleeps.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server `/admin/harness-auth` so the page no longer shows multiple xterm panels. Harness status and apply output now render as plain text, and the **Live authentication terminal** is the only interactive terminal, mounted only while an authentication session is running.\n\n-   Renamed Agents Server standalone VPS harness authentication to `/admin/harness-auth`, with Harness Auth menu/page/API copy and installer guidance aligned around `PTBK_HARNESS` subscription-backed CLI sign-in.\n\n-   Fixed the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal avatar so the sample now uses the shared terminal avatar renderer and the same `AsciiOctopus` fallback as the real Promptbook Developer coder agent. The terminal avatar dimensions and refresh cadence are centralized in `src/utils/agents/terminalAgentAvatarVisual`, with both the real rich CLI UI and the landing page using that shared preset.\n\n-   Fixed `scripts/repair-imports/repair-imports.ts` so it preserves imports from modules mocked in the same test file. The repair pass now detects static `jest.mock(...)` and `vi.mock(...)` module specifiers and leaves matching imports on their mocked facade module instead of redirecting them to deeper implementation files, preventing repaired imports from bypassing test mocks.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server `/admin/task-manager` self-update rows so a successful standalone VPS self-update is no longer shown as failed when the old server process is stopped before the installer writes its final `STATUS=succeeded`. Task-manager self-update snapshots now reuse the same restart-aware target-commit reconciliation as `/admin/update`, and the archived self-update task history stores that resolved success state before a later update overwrites the singleton status file.\n\n-   Updated the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal so it now plays a one-shot `ptbk coder run` sample that mirrors the real rich CLI dashboard: typed command, shared animated agent visual rendered as colored terminal text, `Session` / `Current task` / `Live output` / `Controls` boxes, and final output without blinking, clearing, or looping. The terminal avatar now uses the shared avatar-to-ASCII rendering pipeline instead of a landing-only drawing.\n\n-   Added the `ptbk coder` landing page app at `apps/coder-landing` (http://localhost:4025/). The dark-mode, mobile-friendly Next.js page introduces `ptbk coder` to developers who know Claude Code or OpenAI Codex: copyable syntax-highlighted terminal samples walk from `npm install ptbk` through `ptbk coder init` to the kanban `ptbk coder server`, an animated fake terminal replays a scripted coding session, the `--agent agents/developer.book` option is demonstrated with the default developer agent in a readonly `<BookEditor/>`, and all six harnesses (`claude-code`, `openai-codex`, `github-copilot`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cline`) are presented as cards with logos, model examples, and shell samples. The footer mirrors https://www.ptbk.io/en and states that `ptbk coder` is a Promptbook subproduct by AI Web s.r.o. The app follows the official Promptbook branding and ships with an `apps/coder-landing/specs/` folder of interlinked markdown specs which serve as the single source of truth for 1:1 replication of the page.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server chat source chip for attached images so it shows the original filename (for example `DSC_0139 (2).JPG`) instead of unreadable binary content. Attached files are cited by their content-addressed CDN URL, whose filename is normalized, so the shared citation-label resolver used to download the image and print its first decoded line. Both the durable and private-mode chat surfaces now wrap the resolver with `createAttachmentAwareCitationLabelResolver`, which maps a citation whose URL points to one of the chat attachments back to that attachment's original `name` and only otherwise delegates to the server metadata resolver — which also avoids the needless image download.\n\n-   Fixed `scripts/repair-imports/repair-imports.ts` so cross-boundary imports from `src` to `apps/agents-server/src` can be repaired. The shared project entity scanner can now include app source exports when requested, which lets the repair script resolve Agents Server constants such as `DEFAULT_LOCAL_AGENT_RUNNER_MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS` without broadening the files it rewrites.\n\n-   Added automatic standalone VPS self-updates for the Agents Server. `/admin/update` now exposes `.env`-backed automatic update settings for `PTBK_AUTO_SELF_UPDATE_ENABLED`, `PROMPTBOOK_REPOSITORY_REF`, and `PTBK_AUTO_SELF_UPDATE_CRON` (default `0 0 * * *`) while reusing the shared VPS environment writer used by `/admin/environment`. A Node-runtime scheduler checks the configured branch on the cron cadence and starts the existing zero-downtime self-update flow only when the remote branch is ahead. Persisted self-update jobs now record whether they were started manually or automatically, and both `/admin/update` and `/admin/task-manager` show that trigger.\n\n-   Refactored `ptbk agent-folder run-multiple` so `runMultipleAgentMessages` is now a small watch-loop orchestrator. Active queued-message scheduling, local project summary loading, GitHub repository synchronization, idle auto-pull state, shared dashboard presentation, and path/wait helpers now live in focused private modules under `runMultipleAgentMessages/`, while the exported API, queue selection behavior, retry handling, auto-clone/auto-pull timing, console output, and rich UI state remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server standalone VPS self-update utility so `vpsSelfUpdate` is now a small facade. Environment resolution, `.env`/origin configuration, status/log-file persistence, background process launch, overview assembly, git repository reads, candidate commit listing, and stale-job reconciliation now live in focused private modules under `vpsSelfUpdate/`. The exported API, installer invocation, persisted status/log format, update overview payload, and custom commit picker behavior remain unchanged.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat image attachments so clicking an attached image opens an in-chat popup preview instead of navigating to a new browser tab. Non-image attachments still keep the existing new-tab file link behavior.\n\n-   Added `?messageDraft=` quick buttons to Agents Server chat messages alongside the existing `?message=` buttons. A `[Label](?message=...)` button still sends its text immediately, while a new `[Label](?messageDraft=...)` button prefills the composer with an editable draft — focusing the input and moving the caret to the end — so the text can be reviewed and changed before sending. The markdown button parser now recognizes the `messageDraft` link, `<Chat/>` owns the composer prefill through a new internal draft channel (overridable via the new `onQuickMessageDraftButton` prop), and draft buttons are only shown when there is a composer (or handler) to receive the draft.\n\n-   Fixed the `ptbk coder run` rich terminal UI so sessions started with `--limit <run-count>` now show that configured run limit in the Session scope summary.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server Shibboleth authentication utility so `shibbolethAuthentication` is now a small facade. The SAML protocol/user constants, shared type contracts, RelayState sanitization and request-detail extraction, configuration resolution (Service Provider URL derivation and Identity Provider metadata fetching and XML parsing), Node-SAML client and Service Provider metadata generation, SAML profile-attribute extraction, prefixed table-name resolvers, authentication-attempt audit logging, and user/identity linking now live in focused sibling modules under `shibbolethAuthentication/`. The re-exported functions and types, the SAML request/response handling, the emitted Service Provider metadata, and the observable authentication and audit behavior remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server admin task-manager loader so `getAdminChatTasks` is now a small facade. The SQLite-mode fallback path (raw job/timeout row and user/agent lookup loading, record mapping, in-memory view/search filtering, dashboard sorting, and summary counters) and the PostgreSQL raw-SQL path (the shared union query, the list and counters query builders, and SQL row/counter mapping), together with the shared ISO-timestamp helpers and SQL value coercion, now live in focused sibling modules under `getAdminChatTasks/`. The exported `getAdminChatTasks` signature and `GetAdminChatTasksData` type, the SQLite/PostgreSQL dispatch, the emitted SQL, and the observable task items, counters, and pagination remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server server backup ZIP builder so `createServerBackupZipStream` is now a small facade. The shared lazy-loading Supabase context and table loaders, the section dispatcher and per-section exporters (metadata, agents, conversations, users, files, and messages), the manifest builder, the user/agent preview maps, attachment reference indexing, feedback-thread parsing, wallet redaction, binary download, filename generation, and the generic row/value utilities now live in focused sibling modules under `serverBackup/`. The exported `createServerBackupZipStream` signature, the archive layout, the `promptbook-server-backup/v2` manifest, and the observable ZIP contents remain unchanged.\n\n-   Added `--limit <candidate-count>` to `ptbk coder find-refactor-candidates`, so a single run creates at most that many refactor prompts and, when more candidates are found, keeps only the most important ones. Importance is a combined severity score — the sum of `actual / threshold` ratios across every exceeded line-count, entity-count, function-count, and complexity threshold — computed while scanning, so files that overshoot more thresholds (or overshoot them further) are preferred. The limit is applied after skipping candidates that already have prompts and can be combined with `--level`. The positive-integer option parser previously private to `ptbk coder run` was extracted into a shared `createPositiveIntegerOptionParser` reused by both commands, and the VS Code \"Find refactor candidates for Coding Agent\" terminal now passes `--limit 10`.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server local SQLite Supabase adapter so `$provideLocalSqliteSupabase` is now a small facade. The table-schema metadata and resolvers, value serialization/deserialization, mutation payload defaults, PostgREST filter translation, table/index DDL, row-level DML, SQLite error normalization, low-level SQL helpers, and the Supabase-shaped client/table/query-builder classes now live in focused sibling modules under `localSqliteSupabase/`. The public `$provideLocalSqliteSupabase`, `$resetLocalSqliteSupabaseForTests`, and `ensureLocalSqliteTableReadIndexes` exports, the generated SQL, and the observable query behavior remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server mocked-chats editor state so `useMockedChatsEditorState` is now a lean state orchestrator. Preset cloning, saved-list lookup/upsert/dirty comparison, list persistence and error resolution, delete confirmation, draft save-flow factories, and the participant/message/settings draft reducers now live in focused sibling modules. The API calls, request payloads, feedback messages, draft mutation behavior, and the `UseMockedChatsEditorState` contract remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server export-as-transpiled-code page client so `AgentCodePageClient` is now a small page orchestrator.
