The API calls, request payloads, abort/cleanup behavior, error/loading states, and visible UI remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server standalone VPS update client so `/admin/update` now separates overview polling, target environment controls, current deployment metrics, pending commits, and update-job log/status rendering into focused private helpers. The update POST payloads, polling behavior, success/error messages, and visible UI behavior remain unchanged while the top-level `<UpdateClient/>` is now a small page orchestrator.\n\n-   Enhanced Agents Server chat dictation with a failover-backed speech-to-text flow and Wispr Flow-inspired correction loop. The chat input now keeps microphone states clear through start, stop, processing, permission, and error transitions; preserves the original selection for replace-selection dictation; keeps interim transcript text outside the textarea so the caret stays stable; lets corrections update the local custom-word dictionary including capitalization-only fixes; and backtracks only the tracked dictated chunk instead of restoring the whole previous composer value. The provider layer now reports terminal stall failures when no fallback remains, while the existing OpenAI transcription provider and Browser Web Speech fallback stay behind the shared speech-to-text provider abstraction.\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server homepage graph layout so server, folder, and agent subsets are placed by a deterministic free layout instead of nested grids. The current server is now centered in the graph, folders and agents keep their React Flow parent boundaries, and inheritance/import/team links are used as layout hints at the server, folder, and agent levels so relationship arrows can pass cleanly through the subset boundaries without flattening the hierarchy.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server local and external chat-runner queueing so attached files are visible to the answering agent. Runner `.book` files now include the existing chat attachment context for user messages, preserving image/file URLs and best-effort inline text previews for readable attachments before the local or git-backed runner writes the final answer.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server agent inheritance so local parent agents are loaded directly from the server collection instead of re-entering the authenticated `/api/book` HTTP route. `FROM @Basic` / `FROM {Basic}` now materializes the referenced local parent, agents without `FROM` inherit from the local Adam agent, and `FROM @Void` / `FROM {Void}` still explicitly disables inheritance.\n\n-   Added security PRDs for current Agents Server risks that still need implementation: unauthenticated browser-test automation APIs, missing owner-scoped private agent/folder authorization, and unauthenticated CDN uploads.\n\n-   Leveraged the `spaceTrim` utility for authored multiline strings that were still assembled via array `.join('\\n')` or `+ '\\n\\n' +` concatenation. The `TEAM` commitment's shared teammate-usage guidance, the built-in `ptbk coder` boilerplate template contents, and the `<LlmChatPreview/>` fallback scenario greeting now use `spaceTrim` template literals — producing byte-identical output while improving readability. The now-unused `buildCoderPromptTemplateContent` helper was removed.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk -v` so it prints the Promptbook version just like `ptbk --version`, while keeping `-v` / `--verbose` available for subcommands that use verbose logging. Added VS Code terminal shortcuts for both version checks.\n\n-   Replaced frozen citation page-preview screenshots in Agents Server chat with live browser previews for sources that cannot be embedded in an iframe. The shared `<CitationIframePreview/>` now opens a Playwright-backed MJPEG stream through `/api/page-preview/stream`, forwards click and wheel input through `/api/page-preview/input`, and keeps the existing iframe path for embeddable URLs. Active live preview sessions are tracked in process memory, closed when the modal stream is aborted, and surfaced as `Browser preview` rows in `/admin/task-manager` without a database migration.\n\n-   Surfaced the standalone VPS self-update session triggered from `/admin/update` as a task row inside the Agents Server admin `/admin/task-manager` dashboard. The task-manager API now reads the persisted self-update job snapshot via a new lightweight `readVpsSelfUpdateJobSnapshot` helper (no git access, safe for admin polling), maps it into an `AdminChatTaskRecord` of the new `VPS_SELF_UPDATE` kind through the shared `mapVpsSelfUpdateJobToAdminChatTask` utility, and prepends the synthetic row to page 1 whenever it matches the requested view/search. The row is labelled \"Self-update\", counts toward the running / failed-24h summary metrics, and hides the row-level Cancel/Retry buttons because the self-update lifecycle is driven from `/admin/update` rather than the durable chat-task admin API.\n\n-   Changed the Agents Server footer's \"Made with ❤️ in Europe\" line to show a deterministic positive/neutral emoji derived from the deployment commit hash. The footer now passes the commit-specific emoji through the existing translation placeholder, with a shared `getCommitFooterEmoji` helper and unit coverage for missing SHA fallback, deterministic mapping, and variation across commit hashes.\n-   Changed the Agents Server footer version line to show the latest server release tag, the deployed commit short hash when the server is newer than that tag, and the release age linked to the Git repository. The footer now receives cached server-side Git metadata reused from the self-update helpers, keeping the client footer render lightweight.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server local and external chat-runner queueing so the runner-visible message book for the first durable user turn is assembled through one shared lifecycle helper that prepends the configured `INITIAL MESSAGE` agent greeting and then includes the current `MESSAGE @User` turn. This keeps the synthetic greeting shown in empty chats available to out-of-process runners even though it is not persisted in `UserChat.messages`, while avoiding duplicate local/external thread-building logic.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server initial book seeding so bundled default and `.core` books honor their own `META VISIBILITY` commitment. The standalone seeder and managed-server bootstrap transaction now omit the explicit default visibility override and let the shared persistence normalization resolve the visibility from the book source first, falling back to `UNLISTED` only when the book does not declare it.\n\n-   Hid Agents Server folders whose name starts with `.` (for example `.core`) from the homepage agents list by default, and added a toolbar **Show hidden** / **Hide hidden** toggle so administrators can opt back into seeing them. The new `filterHiddenFolderTree` utility removes hidden folders together with their descendants and the agents inside them in one pass, so the LIST, GRAPH, OFFICE, MAZE, and PIXEL_OFFICE views stay consistent. The toggle state is persisted in the URL as `hidden=show` (mirroring the existing `view=` query pattern) and the toggle button only appears when the unfiltered organization snapshot actually contains a hidden folder, so workspaces without any `.`-prefixed folder are unaffected.\n\n-   Bumped the default coding model used by the `coder:run` npm script created by `ptbk coder init` from `gpt-5.4` to `gpt-5.5`. The bundled `agents/developer.book` (copied into the consumer project from `agents/default/developer.book` via the existing CLI runtime-asset path resolution in `ensureCoderDeveloperAgentFile`) and the automatic post-init boilerplate generation are unchanged; only the `--model` flag baked into the generated script is updated, so `npm run coder:run` now drives OpenAI Codex with `gpt-5.5` by default.\n\n-   Removed the placeholder **\"Working on your request\"** title and the **\"What I'm Doing Now:\"** wrapper from Agents Server durable chat progress cards so the response no longer shows generic headings between the `THINKING_MESSAGES` rotation and the final answer. The phase-based progress card (`createUserChatProgressCard`), the in-process harness progress card (`createUserChatHarnessProgressCard`), and the `agent_progress` tool's default title fallback no longer set the literal `'Working on your request'` heading; the existing `now`/`next`/`items` real-state markdown still renders, with `now` shown directly instead of under a generic label, and the title field stays optional so agents can still supply their own meaningful heading through `agent_progress`.\n\n-   Fixed `<BookEditor/>` TEAM syntax highlighting so inline email addresses like `team@foo.bar` stay plain text while compact teammate references such as `@Paul` and `{Erik Smith}` remain highlighted and linked.\n\n-   Hid non-actionable `{Void}` inheritance and `Time` capability chips from Agents Server homepage agent cards. The underlying agent capabilities and runtime behavior are unchanged; `{Void}` still resolves as an explicit no-parent marker and `USE TIME` still enables time access, but these labels no longer take space in compact card badges.\n\n-   Made standalone VPS Agents Server self-updates more tolerant of intermittent `next-build exited with code null` failures. CLI-owned `ptbk agents-server build` runs now pass a conservative `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_BUILD_WORKER_COUNT=1` into the Agents Server Next config so static analysis/prerender workers do not scale with VPS CPU count while the old pm2 server is still serving traffic. The build wrapper now also retries once when the Next build child is killed by the operating system (for example `SIGKILL` from memory pressure) and reports a branded markdown error with the exit code, signal, and attempt count instead of the vague `code null` message.\n\n-   Sped up Agents Server local chat message handling by allowing the foreground local agent runner to run up to 3 harness instances in parallel by default, exposed as the new `LOCAL_AGENT_RUNNER_MAX_PARALLEL_MESSAGES` setting on `/admin/limits`. The Agents Server launcher now loads this limit together with the local runner retry cap and passes it into `ptbk agent-folder run-multiple`, whose scheduler keeps polling for newly queued files while earlier harness tasks are still running so a fresh message can start without waiting for the previous answer to finish. Local runner queue filenames now include the durable chat job id, preventing concurrent turns in the same chat from overwriting one another, and the server-side local queue mirroring no longer blocks behind an incomplete previous assistant placeholder.\n\n-   Fixed standalone VPS Agents Server self-update leaving multiple `promptbook-agents-server-*` pm2 processes online after partial failures (and even after some successful runs). The blue/green `self_update_agents_server` flow in `other/vps/install.sh` only stopped the immediately previous `old_app_name`, so any orphan left behind by an earlier failed run kept restarting forever via pm2's exponential backoff — wasting RAM/CPU and breaking the \"single instance\" invariant required for a clean `pm2 resurrect` after VPS reboot. The installer now ships a `cleanup_orphan_agents_server_pm2_processes` helper that uses `pm2 jlist` to enumerate every process matching `${PTBK_PM2_BASE_APP_NAME}` / `${PTBK_PM2_BASE_APP_NAME}-*` and deletes everything except the one instance currently serving traffic, then calls `pm2 save` so the systemd-managed `pm2 resurrect` boot path persists exactly one Agents Server process. The new helper runs in three places: at the start of `self_update_agents_server` (sweeps orphans left behind by previous failed runs before any new work begins), in the \"already installed\" shortcut (so re-running the same target also converges to one instance), and at the end of the successful self-update path (running right after the existing `stop_pm2_process_if_running \"$old_app_name\"` so any leftover sibling instance is also removed). A new `SELF_UPDATE_ACTIVE_APP_NAME` global tracks the blue/green hand-off so the `write_failed_self_update_status_on_exit` trap can also run the same cleanup — keeping the old instance if nginx had not switched yet, or keeping the new one if nginx had already moved to the replacement port — meaning a failed `/admin/update` no longer leaves pm2 in a multi-instance state either.\n\n-   Added `META VISIBILITY` as the book-language source of truth for Agents Server agent visibility. Agent creation, book saves, menu visibility changes, and management API visibility updates now normalize the commitment to `PRIVATE`, `UNLISTED`, or `PUBLIC` and mirror it into the database column used for filtering. Bundled default agents now declare their visibility in book source, with `Generic chatter` public and the other defaults private.\n\n-   Added `--limit <run-count>` to `ptbk coder run`, letting coding-agent sessions stop cleanly after the configured number of successful prompt runs. The legacy `run-codex-prompts` option parser now accepts the same flag, and the VS Code terminal list includes a prepared Codex/Claude zig-zag script that runs one prompt per harness with `--limit 1`.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server admin user responses so `/api/users`, `/api/users/[username]`, and the Shibboleth admin dashboard no longer expose `passwordHash`. User-facing code now shares an explicit public user projection and `toPublicUser` mapper, while authentication and password-change paths use narrow internal projections only where the hash is needed.\n\n-   Hardened Agents Server `/api/emails/incoming/sendgrid` against forged SendGrid Inbound Parse callbacks. The route now reads the raw multipart body first, requires a configured `SENDGRID_INBOUND_PARSE_PUBLIC_KEY` (or `SENDGRID_INBOUND_PARSE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` for HMAC deployments), validates the SendGrid signature headers before `formData()` parsing, rejects stale timestamps outside a 5-minute replay window, and only accepts callbacks delivered through `SENDGRID_INBOUND_PARSE_HOSTS`. Invalid or misconfigured callbacks now fail before `parseInboundSendgridEmail` can turn caller-supplied sender/recipient data into inbound `EMAIL` rows in the `Message` table.\n\n-   Hardened Agents Server password authentication against online guessing. `/api/auth/login`, the existing server-action login path, and `/api/auth/change-password` now share a per-process authentication attempt limiter that tracks failed attempts by request IP, username, and `(IP, username)` pair. Repeated failures trigger exponential backoff, excessive failures in the sliding window return `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After`, and every failed, successful, and rate-limited password check is logged with the requesting IP for forensics.\n\n-   Hardened Agents Server `/api/chat/export/pdf` against unauthenticated and SSRF-style abuse. The route now requires `getCurrentUser()` before reading the payload, applies a per-user sliding-window rate limit before spawning Playwright, sanitizes generated chat-export HTML URL attributes through the existing `assertSafeUrl` guard before rendering, blocks all Chromium network requests except non-network `about:` / `data:` URLs during PDF generation, and returns `Content-Disposition` with a quoted ASCII fallback plus RFC 5987 `filename*` encoding.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server durable chat progress so users see real progress in the requested sequence instead of an immediate synthetic queued card:\n\n    -   Newly queued assistant placeholders no longer persist a progress card, which lets the browser rotate the configured `THINKING_MESSAGES` while the worker has not picked up the job yet.\n    -   When the local or external agent runner actually receives the request, the assistant placeholder now remains on the browser-side `THINKING_MESSAGES` rotation until the final answer is ready.\n    -   The in-process streaming runner path now derives one visible harness update from streamed tool-call snapshots, reusing the same hidden-tool filtering as chat chips so `agent_progress` / `assistant_preparation` stay internal while real actions surface as **\"Running action: Searching the web.\"** or **\"Action completed: Browsing the web.\"**\n    -   The final answer still replaces the progress surface as before, and progress text summarizes user-facing actions/results without exposing hidden chain-of-thought, raw tool payloads, secrets, or technical logs.\n\n-   Fixed `\\`headers\\` was called outside a request scope`crash during the standalone VPS Agents Server installation. The bundled-default-agents step runs the`seedDefaultAgents.ts`script via`tsx`outside any Next.js request, but`seedCoreAgents`reached for table names through`$getTableName('Agent')` / `$getTableName('AgentFolder')`, which transitively called `$provideServer()` → `next/headers#headers()` and threw on the bare CLI. The two internal helpers (`loadExistingActiveAgentNames` and `ensureCoreFolderExists`) now accept the `tablePrefix` already resolved by `seedCoreAgents` from `options.tablePrefix ?? process.env.SUPABASE_TABLE_PREFIX ?? ''` and build the prefixed `Agent` / `AgentFolder` table names directly, mirroring the synchronous concatenation pattern used by `AgentCollectionInSupabase.getTableName`. The Next.js-request-scoped `$getTableName`import is dropped from`seedCoreAgents.ts`, so the standalone seeder no longer touches request-scope APIs — request-handling code paths keep using `$getTableName`unchanged. The companion`registerServerErrorSentryLogging.test.ts`\"keeps logging locally when Sentry is not configured\" case is also tightened to clear`NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`along with`SENTRY_DSN`(and to restore it in`afterEach`), because `resolveOptionalSentryDsn`falls back to the public DSN — the previous test passed only on machines without a populated`.env`, and the local `npm run test-for-ptbk-coder` verification surfaced it.\n\n-   Removed the unauthenticated infinite-stream DoS endpoint `/api/long-streaming` from Agents Server. The route opened a `ReadableStream` and pushed a single byte every 100 ms inside a `while (just(true))` loop with no termination condition, no `request.signal` abort handling, no authentication, and no rate limit, so any anonymous client could hold one (or many) connections open indefinitely to consume Node's event-loop, HTTP keep-alive slots, and reverse-proxy connection budget on the standalone VPS deployment — a denial-of-service primitive that needed **zero** authentication or skill to exploit. The endpoint was a leftover demo / test route with no caller anywhere in the Agents Server frontend or in the rest of the repository, so deleting the `apps/agents-server/src/app/api/long-streaming/` folder closes the attack surface entirely without removing any real feature.\n\n-   Fixed two internal shared-secret tokens reusing `ADMIN_PASSWORD` and other unrelated secrets in Agents Server. Both `resolveUserChatWorkerInternalToken` (which protects the internal background-worker routes `/api/internal/user-chat-jobs/run`, `/api/internal/user-chat-timeouts/run`, and `/api/internal/agent-runner-limits`) and `resolveTeamInternalAgentAccessToken` (which authorizes same-server `TEAM` calls into private teammate agents) fell back to a chain of unrelated environment variables when their dedicated `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_USER_CHAT_WORKER_TOKEN` / `PROMPTBOOK_TEAM_AGENT_ACCESS_TOKEN` variable was missing. The worker-token chain in particular ended in a publicly-known constant (`'promptbook-user-chat-worker'`), so an operator who deployed without explicitly configuring the variable left the gate effectively open — anyone who computed `sha256('user-chat-worker:promptbook-user-chat-worker')` could drive jobs at will. Even on the \"good\" path, deriving the worker token from `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` or `ADMIN_PASSWORD` meant leaking either secret leaked the worker token and vice versa.\n\n    Both functions now require their dedicated environment variable and never fall back to `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`, or any hardcoded literal — matching the existing `SESSION_SECRET`, `GITHUB_APP_STATE_SECRET`, and `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_STATE_SECRET` patterns so all \"must be a dedicated secret\" stories share one approach:\n\n    -   `resolveUserChatWorkerInternalToken` caches the value resolved from `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_USER_CHAT_WORKER_TOKEN` on first use. In production it throws a clear `EnvironmentMismatchError` (with the same `spaceTrim` markdown format as the existing `SESSION_SECRET` guard) instead of silently using a shared credential, and outside production it generates a per-process random token via `crypto.randomBytes(32)` and warns once — so local development keeps working without configuration while still rejecting the unsafe fallback chain.\n    -   `resolveTeamInternalAgentAccessToken` now only reads `PROMPTBOOK_TEAM_AGENT_ACCESS_TOKEN`; when the variable is missing it returns `null` so the existing `createTeamInternalAgentAccessHeaders` and `isTeamInternalAgentAccessToken` guards already in place fail closed — same-server team access is simply disabled and no header is sent (or accepted) instead of silently authorizing requests with the wrong secret.\n    -   Updated the deployment plumbing so a fresh standalone VPS installation does not require manual configuration: `other/vps/install.sh` now calls `ensure_secret_env_value PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_USER_CHAT_WORKER_TOKEN 32` and `ensure_secret_env_value PROMPTBOOK_TEAM_AGENT_ACCESS_TOKEN 32` next to the existing `SESSION_SECRET` generator, so both secrets are auto-provisioned with `openssl rand -hex 32` on first boot and persisted into the installed `.env`. The two new keys were also added to `VPS_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_KEYS` so administrators can rotate them from the VPS UI, to `ptbk agents-server init` so the local scaffold writes documented placeholders, to the root `.env.example`, and to the Agents Server e2e harness so Playwright tests run with dedicated values that differ from the admin password.\n    -   Documented both variables in `apps/agents-server/README.md` next to `SESSION_SECRET` (anchors `agents-server-env-ptbk-agents-server-user-chat-worker-token` and `agents-server-env-promptbook-team-agent-access-token`) and removed the misleading \"If unset, `ADMIN_PASSWORD` will be used as a fallback\" note from `env-manual/GITHUB_APP.md` so the operator-facing docs no longer endorse credential reuse.\n\n-   Fixed timing attack vulnerability in Agents Server secret and token comparisons. Three additional comparison sites (the signed-session HMAC signature in `parseSessionToken`, the same-server TEAM access token in `isTeamInternalAgentAccessToken`, and the shared internal worker token in the `/api/internal/agent-runner-limits` and `/api/internal/user-chat-jobs/run` routes) used JavaScript's `===` / `!==` operators, which short-circuit on the first byte that differs and let a remote attacker who can measure response timing recover each secret one byte at a time. All three sites now share a new `isTimingSafeEqualString` utility (in `src/utils/`) that calls Node.js's `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length `Buffer`s and returns `false` immediately on length mismatch (which only leaks length, not content). The helper tolerates `null` / `undefined` inputs so callers can forward raw request values without an extra guard, and the session-cookie comparison stays compatible with legacy tokens because both sides are still derived from the same `HMAC-SHA256` hex digest of equal length.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server `/api/internal/user-chat-jobs/run` looping back-to-back forever when an old `FAILED` local chat job still had its `failed` message-folder book on disk. `synchronizeLocalUserChatJob` was re-marking such jobs as `FAILED` on every tick, which set `didMutate: true` and caused the worker route's `after()` self-requeue to fire immediately. The failed-file branch now mirrors the existing timeout-branch guard (`job.status !== 'FAILED'`), so already-failed jobs short-circuit to `waiting` instead of being re-persisted, and the route stops requeueing itself.\n\n-   Extended standalone VPS Agents Server non-interactive installation:\n\n    -   Added the explicit `--yes-i-understand-that-script-should-be-run-on-fresh-server` installer option alongside `PTBK_CONFIRM_FRESH_VPS=yes`, so automated installs can acknowledge the fresh-server requirement without an interactive prompt.\n    -   Added installer options for the common automated values (`--domain`, `--openai-api-key`, `--sentry-dsn`, and `--admin-password`) while reusing the same defaults and environment variables as the interactive prompts.\n    -   Documented interactive and non-interactive standalone VPS installation examples in the README, including the non-interactive harness skip behavior.\n\n-   Replaced the remote Promptbook Core Agents Server with a bundled local `.core` folder so each Agents Server can run without any external dependency on `core.ptbk.io`:\n\n    -   Removed the `CORE_AGENTS_SERVER` constant from `servers.ts` along with the `CORE_SERVER` and `IS_CORE_SERVER_HIDDEN` metadata defaults; new servers no longer point at a special core federated server and federated servers are now all equal.\n    -   Added a new bundled `.core/` subfolder under `agents/default/` containing the well-known `adam.book` and `teacher.book` (plus other built-in core agents). Default-agent seeding now also seeds these books into a database `.core` folder via the new shared `seedCoreAgents` helper (reused by both the standalone `seedDefaultAgents` runtime path and the managed-server bootstrap transaction through the new `seedServerCoreAgents` companion).\n    -   On every server start (and after every default-agent install), the seeder auto-creates the `.core` folder when missing and inserts any well-known core agent (Adam, Teacher, …) that is not already present, regardless of the visibility set on the bundled book — so Adam is always available as the implicit ancestor for every agent.\n    -   `getWellKnownAgentUrl` now returns the URL of the local well-known agent on the current Agents Server origin (`/agents/adam`, `/agents/teacher`, …) instead of resolving the deprecated `CORE_SERVER` metadata, so `FROM {Adam}`, the Teacher remote agent, and custom-domain Adam fallback all stay inside the current server.\n    -   Removed the now-obsolete `defaultFederatedAgents` background sync (`scheduleDefaultFederatedAgentsSync`, `synchronizeDefaultFederatedAgents`, `fetchCoreOrganizationPayload`, …) that copied default boilerplate agents from `CORE_SERVER` into every new server; the local `.core` seeder fully replaces it.\n    -   `getFederatedServers` no longer special-cases a hidden core server; it just returns the user-configured `FEDERATED_SERVERS` list (empty by default), and the `excludeHiddenCoreServer` option was dropped from its three call sites (homepage layout, federated agents API, federated search provider).\n\n-   Added Agents Server agents import/export on the agents listing:\n\n    -   Admins can download `{server-name}.agents.zip`, containing `.book` files directly in the agents folder structure so importing it into a fresh server recreates the agents and folders.\n    -   Admins can import dropped or selected `.book` files and ZIP archives; ZIP folder structure is embedded under the currently open folder, non-book ZIP entries trigger a proceed warning and are ignored, same-book duplicates are skipped, and different-book duplicate names ask whether to import duplicates or skip conflicts.\n\n-   Added standalone metadata import/export to the Agents Server `/admin/metadata` page:\n\n    -   Admins can now download a `{server-name}.metadata.json` file containing the Promptbook version and only metadata values/notes that differ from built-in defaults.\n    -   Admins can import that JSON into another server; omitted built-in metadata fields resolve to current defaults, so exporting a configured server and importing into a fresh server recreates the metadata configuration without bundling full server data.\n    -   Metadata imports from `/admin/metadata` now ask admins for each imported metadata key whether to keep the current value or use the imported value, and skipped entries preserve the current server configuration instead of resetting omitted built-in defaults.\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server `/admin/update` super-admin page so it shows richer context before, during, and after a standalone VPS self-update — making it easier to decide when to update and to debug a failed update:\n\n    -   `readVpsSelfUpdateOverview` now also returns a `pendingCommits` list (subject, short/full commit hash, author timestamp) for the commits between the currently deployed checkout and the latest commit on the configured branch, capped at 100 entries so a long-stale server still responds quickly. A new `<PendingCommitsCard/>` renders that list together with the existing `X commits behind · Y time behind` drift summary, so the admin can review exactly what is about to be installed.\n    -   The overview now performs a best-effort fetch of the tracked remote branch before calculating update drift, then returns the latest remote commit subject/date/hash from the local object database when available. The current and latest commit cards, plus every pending-commit row, now visibly show the commit subject, full hash, and authored date.\n    -   Factored the time-behind suffix out of `buildDeploymentDriftLabel` into a new shared `buildDeploymentTimeBehindLabel` helper so the same localized `N days behind` text powers both the current-deployment card and the pending-commits card without duplication.\n    -   Added a new `GET /api/admin/update/log` route that streams the full persisted `self-update.log` file (gated by `isUserGlobalAdmin`) together with a `Content-Disposition` filename, backed by a new `readVpsSelfUpdateLogFileContent` helper in `vpsSelfUpdate.ts`.\n    -   When the latest update job's status is `failed`, the Update job card now shows **Copy log** and **Download log** buttons that hit the new endpoint and reuse the shared `downloadBlob` / `parseFilenameFromContentDisposition` helpers (same flow as the existing Backup export), so the admin can quickly share the full installer log with the developers for debugging instead of only seeing the truncated terminal tail.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server `/admin/update` self-update failing on the standalone VPS during the post-compile `Linting and checking validity of types ...` phase with `next-build exited with code null.` (the Node build process was being killed by the OS, typically by the OOM killer, after webpack had already retried minification multiple times). The shared `other/vps/install.sh` `build_agents_server` step now sets `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_IGNORE_NEXT_VALIDATION=true` so the VPS production build skips the duplicate Next.js lint + TypeScript validation step that is already enforced by repository CI, matching the existing CLI materialized-runtime build path and letting the self-update finish reliably on memory-constrained VPS hosts.\n\n-   Changed the Agents Server durable chat progress card so each preparation phase shows the **real runtime state** that has actually been resolved so far, instead of a fixed scripted blurb that was identical for every chat turn:\n\n    -   `createUserChatProgressCard` now accepts a `UserChatProgressContext` object and composes the `now`/`next` markdown from real signals — resolved agent name, attachment count, configured tool count and friendly tool labels (e.g. `web browser`, `web search`, `email sending`), knowledge-source count, calendar/email/project integrations, the resolved LLM provider title, and whether the AgentKit runtime came from the in-process cache.\n    -   `createRunUserChatJobExecutionContext` builds that context incrementally as the worker resolves new information and forwards it through `reportProgress` at every phase, so the user sees, for example, **\"Loading the instructions and configured commitments for agent Cooking Coach (2 knowledge sources)\"** instead of the previous static **\"Preparing the agent instructions and context needed for this request.\"**\n    -   The `starting_response` update is now emitted **after** the AgentKit cache lookup completes, so the progress text can name the actual provider (e.g. **\"Calling the language model via OpenAI\"**) and call out whether the agent had to be prepared fresh.\n    -   Added a small `resolveUserChatProgressToolHighlights` helper that maps technical commitment tool identifiers (`web_search`, `useBrowser`, `send_email`, …) to short user-facing labels and excludes the internal `agent_progress` / `assistant_preparation` tools that should never appear as user-relevant capabilities.\n    -   Updated the queued-message lifecycle copy to reflect the actual queueing state (**\"Your message is waiting in the queue for the next available worker to pick it up.\"**) and updated `userChatMessageLifecycle.test.ts` accordingly.\n\n-   Added a new `Octopus 3D 4` built-in avatar visual as a smoother, blobbier continuation of `Octopus 3D 3`, and promoted it to the new shared `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL`:\n\n    -   Reused the seeded `Octopus3` morphology profile together with the shared projected-eye and projected-mouth helpers so the new proper-3D octopus stays consistent with the rest of the octopus family without duplicating face-rendering logic.\n    -   Rendered the whole octopus as one continuous blobby mesh sampled at a higher latitude/longitude resolution so the silhouette reads as a round, real-octopus body with eight tentacle lobes that smoothly fuse into the mantle instead of attaching as separate ribbons.\n    -   Drove the tentacle motion with a combined primary, secondary, and slow-curl sine harmonic per lobe so the tentacles wave naturally and continuously, like a real octopus drifting in water, while remaining cute and simple.\n    -   Added a richer multi-pass shading pipeline (key light, rim light, soft gloss highlight, seeded pigment spots, and per-patch outline) on top of the existing palette tones, so the silhouette feels textured and visually appealing without leaving the simple flat-stylized look.\n    -   Kept avatar pointer tracking on both the full mesh silhouette and the projected eyes — the head turns toward the mouse cursor more responsively than `Octopus 3D 3` and the eyes track the pointer inside the rotated head.\n    -   Switched the shared `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL_ID` to `octopus3d4`, updated the Agents Server `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL` metadata default + allowed-values note to include `OCTOPUS3D4`, and added a backwards-compatible database migration that upgrades existing `OCTOPUS3D3` defaults to `OCTOPUS3D4` while preserving any administrator-customized value.\n\n-   Fixed broken access control on chat history, chat feedback, and agent CRUD routes of Agents Server. Multiple route handlers guarded themselves with `getCurrentUser()` (i.e. \"the caller is logged in\") but never checked that the **specific record** being read, modified, or deleted belonged to the caller or that the caller was an administrator, so any authenticated user — including self-registered unprivileged users — could read, mutate, or destroy data that belonged to other users / other agents:\n\n    -   `/api/chat-history` (`GET`/`DELETE`), `/api/chat-history/[id]` (`DELETE`), `/api/chat-history/export` (`GET`), `/api/chat-feedback` (`GET`/`DELETE`), and `/api/chat-feedback/export` (`GET`) returned (or deleted) the **entire** `ChatHistory` / `ChatFeedback` tables across every agent and user. These endpoints power the admin-only `/admin/chat-history` and `/admin/chat-feedback` screens — which expose IPs, anonymous `userNote`s, and `expectedAnswer`s across all agents — so they are now gated by `isUserAdmin()` instead of `getCurrentUser()`, returning `401 Unauthorized` for non-administrators. The two admin pages and the agent-context-menu entries that link to them were updated to require admin as well, so non-administrators no longer see dead-end links to those screens.\n    -   `PATCH /api/agents/[agentName]` (rename / change visibility) and `DELETE /api/agents/[agentName]` (tombstone) never resolved the agent's owner. Both handlers now resolve the target agent through a new shared `findAgentForCallerWriteAccess` helper that combines `findOwnedAgentByIdentifier` (reusing the same ownership primitive as the v1 management API) with an `isUserAdmin()` admin override, and reject with `404 Not Found` when the agent does not belong to the caller and the caller is not an administrator. The visibility update is now scoped to the resolved row by primary key instead of matching every agent that shares the supplied name or permanent id. The new helper also covers legacy `ADMIN_PASSWORD` administrators that have no database user id.\n\n-   Fixed SSRF vulnerability in three additional Agents Server endpoints that accepted a caller-supplied URL and fetched it server-side without authentication and without the existing `assertSafeUrl` SSRF guard:\n\n    -   `/api/page-preview/screenshot` opened the URL in a headless Playwright browser (which executes JavaScript on the fetched page) and returned a PNG screenshot. The only validation was that the scheme was `http:` or `https:`, so an unauthenticated attacker could screenshot `http://127.0.0.1`, `http://169.254.169.254` (AWS / GCP / Azure metadata service), or any RFC-1918 private address.\n    -   `/api/page-preview/check` performed a server-side `fetch` (HEAD with `redirect: follow`) through `checkIfUrlCanBeEmbedded` with the same lack of validation.\n    -   `/api/team-agent-profile` called `fetchAgentProfile` against any URL that passed the structural `isValidAgentUrl` check and forwarded the internal team access token to the target. The same-origin check inside `createTeamInternalAgentAccessHeaders` already prevented the token from leaking to truly cross-origin URLs, but the SSRF itself was unblocked.\n\n    All three endpoints now require authentication (`getCurrentUser` returns `401 Unauthorized` for anonymous requests) and validate the destination URL through `assertSafeUrl` (the same helper that already protects `/api/scrape`) before any outbound `fetch` / `page.goto`, returning `400 Bad Request` for non-HTTP(S) schemes and private/internal IP destinations (loopback, RFC 1918, link-local / cloud-metadata, shared address space, IPv6 ULA / link-local / loopback). The chat citation iframe-fallback feature is unaffected because it runs inside the authenticated chat UI and previews public citation URLs. The `[👣][🧠]` TODO in `isValidAgentUrl` is resolved by keeping that function a pure structural validator and documenting that callers reaching untrusted networks must apply `assertSafeUrl` themselves.\n\n-   Fixed unauthenticated abuse of server-side paid AI APIs in Agents Server. Five route handlers proxied directly to paid third-party providers (OpenAI, ElevenLabs) using the **server's API keys** without any authentication check, so any anonymous client could drain the configured API credit and exhaust quotas by repeatedly calling them. All five routes are now protected by a new shared `guardPaidApiRequest` utility that combines authentication and per-identity sliding-window rate limiting (DRY for all paid-proxy endpoints):\n\n    -   `/api/chat` and `/api/chat-streaming` were OpenAI smoke-test endpoints with no frontend usage. They are now gated behind `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` and return `404` in production so they cannot be exploited even if the deployment exposes them.\n    -   `/api/openai/v1/audio/transcriptions` now requires authentication (signed session cookie or `Authorization: Bearer ptbk_…` API key), enforces a 25 MB upload size limit, validates the `model` parameter against an allowlist of supported OpenAI transcription models (`gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `whisper-1`), validates `language` against ISO-639-1, and truncates the optional transcription `prompt` to 800 characters.\n    -   `/api/elevenlabs/tts` now requires authentication and validates the caller-supplied `voiceId` against the strict ElevenLabs format (15–40 alphanumeric characters), preventing path-segment injection into the upstream URL and rejecting unknown voices that would still bill the ElevenLabs account.\n    -   `/api/images/[filename]` now requires authentication and validates `modelName`, `size`, `quality`, and `style` query parameters against fixed allowlists (DALL·E / Gemini image models, supported sizes, `standard`/`hd`, `vivid`/`natural`) before forwarding to the paid image generation provider.\n    -   The shared guard applies a per-identity sliding-window rate limit on top of authentication — by username for cookie sessions, by hashed API key for bearer auth, and by request IP for any anonymous fallback. Budgets are tier-specific (60/min for transcription and TTS, 20/min for image generation), so a single compromised account cannot sustain large bills. Rejected requests receive `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header.\n\n-   Fixed authentication bypass in Agents Server `validateApiKey`: the helper previously treated the presence of any `sessionToken` cookie as proof of a valid browser session, so any client could forge `Cookie: sessionToken=anything` and gain unauthenticated access to every endpoint behind `validateApiKey` (including the OpenAI-compatible chat-completion routes that consume server-side API credits). The helper now parses the cookie value with the existing `parseSessionToken` HMAC-signature verifier and only accepts the request when the signature matches, restoring the original intent of the browser-session shortcut without trusting attacker-supplied cookies.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server directory and chat-sidebar reads for standalone VPS and Supabase deployments:\n\n    -   Added SQLite read indexes for active agent/folder directory scans, chat sidebar lists, and active chat job/timeout polling used by the homepage, agent navigation, and chat pages.\n    -   Added matching PostgreSQL indexes for active agent/folder directory reads and creation-time chat sidebar ordering.\n    -   Invalidated cached active organization snapshots after agent source, visibility, create, delete, and restore mutations so optimized homepage/menu data refreshes immediately.\n\n-   Fixed timing attack vulnerability in Agents Server admin password verification: all three comparison sites (`isUserGlobalAdmin`, `getCurrentUser`, `authenticateUser`) now use a shared `isAdminPasswordEqual` utility that calls Node.js's `timingSafeEqual` (from the `crypto` module) instead of JavaScript's `===` operator, preventing character-by-character password inference via response-time measurement.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server durable chat progress so new agent responses show structured real progress from the queued and preparation phases instead of a synthetic immediate pre-answer:\n\n    -   Queued assistant placeholders now render a progress card with current step, next step, and checklist state.\n    -   The durable chat worker updates that card while it reads context, prepares the agent, checks available tools/inputs, and starts the response.\n    -   The `agent_progress` tool instructions now ask the real agent to report concise user-facing decisions, actions, and results without exposing hidden chain-of-thought or raw technical details.\n\n-   Fixed SSRF vulnerability in the Agents Server `/api/scrape` endpoint:\n\n    -   The endpoint now requires authentication — unauthenticated requests receive a `401 Unauthorized` response.\n    -   Added URL validation via a new `assertSafeUrl` utility that rejects non-HTTP(S) schemes and destination hostnames that resolve to private/internal IP ranges (RFC 1918: `10.x`, `172.16–31.x`, `192.168.x`; loopback `127.x`; link-local / cloud-metadata `169.254.x`; shared address space `100.64.x`; IPv6 ULA, link-local, and loopback). Blocked requests receive a `400 Bad Request` response.\n\n-   Fixed package publishing for `@promptbook/cli` by marking the `ptbk coder server` HTTP/UI helpers as CLI-only instead of never-publishable, matching the existing CLI command import chain.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder find-unwritten` command that lists all prompt sections whose body still contains the `@@@` authoring placeholder:\n\n    -   Prints a summary line (done / for agent / to be written counts) followed by a numbered list of unwritten prompts with their file path, line number, and first summary line.\n    -   Accepts `--priority <n>` to apply the same minimum-priority filter used by `ptbk coder run`.\n    -   Reuses the existing `listPromptsToBeWritten` / `printPromptsToBeWritten` utilities so the detection logic stays in one place.\n\n-   Added `--agent <agent-book-path>` option to `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server`:\n\n    -   Accepts a path to a `.book` file (relative to the current working directory) whose compiled system message is prepended to each coding prompt before the task text.\n    -   Can be combined with `--context`: the agent system message is inserted first, followed by the task prompt, and finally the context — so the harness sees agent instructions → task → additional context.\n    -   Example: `ptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --context AGENTS.md --agent agents/coding-expert.book`\n\n-   `ptbk coder init` now automatically generates 5 prompt boilerplate files after setting up the project configuration.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder server` command that runs the same prompt-processing logic as `ptbk coder run` but keeps the process alive and serves a kanban web UI on a configurable port (default `4441`):\n\n    -   The server polls for new prompt files every 5 seconds instead of exiting when all prompts are done or none are ready, making it suitable as a long-running background service.\n    -   A kanban board at `http://localhost:4441` shows all prompt sections grouped into four columns: **To Do**, **Not Ready**, **Done**, and **Failed**.\n    -   Each card is clickable and opens a Trello-style edit modal where the prompt text can be modified and saved back to the source file immediately.\n    -   A **Play / Pause** button in the browser header is kept in sync with the CLI pause state; clicking it calls the same `requestPause` / `requestResume` functions used by the `p` key in the terminal.\n    -   The HTTP server exposes a small REST API: `GET /api/prompts`, `GET /api/status`, `POST /api/pause`, `POST /api/resume`, and `PUT /api/prompts/update`.\n    -   All options from `ptbk coder run` are supported (`--harness`, `--model`, `--thinking-level`, `--context`, `--test`, `--wait`, `--priority`, `--no-commit`, etc.) plus a new `--port` option (or `PTBK_CODER_SERVER_PORT` env var).\n    -   The frontend source lives in `apps/coder-server/index.html` and is served inline by the Node.js HTTP server (no build step required).\n\n-   Added a VSCode extension (`apps/vscode-extension`) for the Book language that provides syntax highlighting for `.book` and `.ptbk` files. The TextMate grammar (`syntaxes/book.tmLanguage.json`) is dynamically generated from `COMMITMENT_REGISTRY` by running `npm run generate-vscode-grammar`, ensuring the extension always reflects the current set of commitment keywords. Publishing to the Visual Studio Code Marketplace is available through `npm run build:vscode-extension -- --publish`, which generates the grammar, syncs a Marketplace-safe extension version from the root `package.json`, publishes with `vsce`, and creates the VSIX artifact.\n\n-   Fixed `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting incorrectly highlighting the local part of email addresses (e.g. `team@foo.bar`) as agent references. `@`-style references now require whitespace or start-of-line before the `@` sign, so only `@Paul` (with preceding whitespace) is highlighted, not `team@foo.bar`. Removed a now-redundant manual preceding-character check that duplicated this logic.\n\n-   Improved `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting to dynamically detect commitments — any line starting with one or more all-uppercase words (minimum 2 characters each) is now highlighted as a commitment keyword, without relying on a hardcoded list of known commitment types. Lines starting with a dash or a single uppercase letter are not affected. Special commitment types (`NOTE`, `NOTES`, `NONCE`, `TODO`) retain their distinct colors, and `FROM`/`IMPORT`/`IMPORTS`/`TEAM` retain agent-reference link highlighting.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server VPS installation failing on the first run with a Node.js out-of-memory crash during the Next.js production build. The `ptbk agents-server build` command now passes `--max-old-space-size=4096` in `NODE_OPTIONS` when spawning the webpack compilation process, allowing the ~1.9 GiB peak heap usage to succeed within the swap-backed memory budget enforced by the installer. Existing `NODE_OPTIONS` values are preserved; the flag is only injected when no `--max-old-space-size` is already set.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server file upload URLs for self-contained S3 to hide the internal bucket name, path prefix, and directory structure. Files are now stored under a content-addressed key (`{hash[0]}/{hash[1]}/{sha256}/{filename}`) and served through a new Next.js proxy route (`/s3/{hex}/{hex}/{hash}/{filename}`) so the public URL is unguessable and reveals no internal storage details. Old-style URLs (e.g. `/s3/promptbook-files/ptbk-agents/user/files/…`) remain accessible for backwards compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed citation source previews in Agents Server chat failing silently when the target page blocks iframe embedding via `X-Frame-Options` (e.g. `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`). The chat modal now checks embeddability server-side before rendering and falls back to a server-taken screenshot with an \"Open in new tab\" link when the page cannot be framed.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server database layer to prevent the server from becoming unresponsive under load:\n\n    -   Added `connectionTimeoutMillis` (15 s) to the shared PostgreSQL connection pool so queries fail fast when all connections are busy instead of queuing indefinitely — the root cause of the server becoming completely unresponsive after a period of high traffic.\n    -   Increased the default pool size from 10 to 20 connections (configurable via `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` environment variable) to handle more concurrent chat-stream polling and atomic-SQL operations without exhausting the pool.\n    -   Added `idleTimeoutMillis` (30 s) and `allowExitOnIdle` so unused connections are closed promptly, keeping memory and socket usage low.\n    -   Added a pool `error` event handler so unexpected errors on idle clients are logged instead of propagating as unhandled exceptions that can corrupt the pool state.\n    -   Added a 30-second hard timeout to every Supabase HTTP request via a custom `fetch` wrapper on the server-side Supabase client. Without this, a slow or temporarily unreachable PostgREST endpoint would cause Supabase queries to hang indefinitely, holding Node.js event-loop resources and contributing to the gradual unresponsiveness over time.\n\n-   Added `isVerbose` option to `CliAgent` so callers can enable the same harness-level console output that `ptbk agent exec --verbose` produces without spawning the CLI. `LiteAgent` already supported `isVerbose`; both classes now expose the option consistently.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat runner not including the agent's initial message (defined via `INITIAL MESSAGE` commitment) in the queued book file when a user sends their first message. The local and external chat runners now prepend the agent's initial message as the opening `MESSAGE @Agent` block so the agent runner sees the full conversation context from the start.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat messages being silently cropped when the agent response contained a line starting with a single uppercase ASCII letter followed by lowercase text (e.g. \"V části...\" in Czech). `Book.parse` was incorrectly treating such lines as commitment headers due to an overly permissive regex in `parseCommitmentHeader`. The fix tightens the regex to require at least two characters in the first keyword word, which prevents common natural-language words like \"V\" (Czech for \"in\") or \"A\" / \"I\" in English from being mistaken for commitment markers.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server chat tray ordering from last-activity time to creation time so chats stay in their chronological position and browsing an older chat no longer moves it to the top of the list.\n\n-   Optimized animated avatar rendering performance in Agents Server to fix 1–2 fps drops when multiple avatars are visible:\n\n    -   Throttled the shared animation loop to ~24 fps (from the display refresh rate of 60 fps+) via a frame-interval gate in `avatarAnimationScheduler.ts`. Animated octopus visuals change slowly enough that 24 fps is perceptually identical to 60 fps while reducing total render work by ~60%.\n    -   Cached stable per-avatar data (morphology profile, animation phase, tentacle profiles, eye phase offsets) using a `WeakMap` keyed on the `createRandom` factory reference in `octopus3dAvatarVisual`, `octopus3d2AvatarVisual`, and `octopus3d3AvatarVisual`. These values are deterministic given the avatar definition and were previously recomputed on every frame.\n    -   Replaced `context.filter = 'blur()'` shadow effects in all six affected visuals (`octopus3d`, `octopus3d2`, `octopus3d3`, `minecraft`, `minecraft2`, `fractal`) with equivalent gradient-based approximations. CSS filter blur forces the browser into a full software rasterization pass on every frame; the gradient alternative is hardware-accelerated and visually equivalent.\n    -   Added `\"ts-node\": { \"transpileOnly\": true }` to `tsconfig.json` so the CLI integration test (`ts-node src/cli/test/ptbk.ts --help`) skips full type-checking during execution. Type correctness is still enforced by the dedicated `test-types` step; this change brings the CLI startup from an uncapped compile pass (> 5 min on Windows) down to ~20 seconds.\n\n-   Further optimized animated avatar rendering performance in Agents Server, building on the earlier 24 fps throttle and stable-state cache. With twelve animated octopus avatars on a single page the previous pass still left the UI at 1–2 fps because every visible avatar fired on the same animation frame and the per-frame mesh sampling cost remained heavy:\n\n    -   Interleaved listeners in `avatarAnimationScheduler.ts` so animated avatars no longer all render on the same animation frame. Each listener now tracks its own last-run timestamp, new listeners are phase-staggered at registration, and the shared loop runs at most `MAX_AVATAR_LISTENERS_PER_FRAME` (= 2) listeners per `requestAnimationFrame`, scheduling the rest on subsequent frames. Each avatar still reaches the 24 fps target individually; total per-frame work is bounded regardless of how many avatars are visible.\n    -   Added per-frame corner-grid sample caching to `octopus3d3AvatarVisual` and `octopus3d2AvatarVisual`. The mesh patch loop previously called `sampleContinuousOctopusSurfacePoint` / `sampleBlobbyOctopusSurfacePoint` for each of the four corners of every patch (16×40×4 = 2 560 samples per frame for `octopus3d3`), even though most corners are shared between neighboring patches. The new implementation precomputes a `(latitudePatchCount + 1) × (longitudePatchCount + 1)` corner grid once per frame, cutting the sample call count by ~3.7× on `octopus3d3` and ~4× on `octopus3d2`.\n    -   Added per-frame longitude caching for `resolveContinuousTentacleInfluence`, `resolveContinuousLobeWave`, and `resolveLowerLobeWave` in the same two visuals. Each tentacle-influence evaluation runs an 8-iteration `Math.exp` loop over the seeded tentacle profiles, so calling it once per longitude grid value instead of once per corner cuts the dominant inner-loop cost by ~30×. The new `sampleContinuousOctopusSurfacePointWithLongitudeCache` / `sampleBlobbyOctopusSurfacePointWithLongitudeCache` helpers accept the cached values explicitly; the existing public sample functions are preserved for off-grid callers (eyes, mouth).\n\n-   Added `--wait [duration]` flag to `ptbk coder run` for controlling the delay between prompt rounds:\n\n    -   `--wait 1h` (or `--wait 30m`, `--wait 5s`, combinations like `--wait 1h30m`) waits the specified duration between rounds to avoid hitting harness rate limits. The first prompt executes immediately; the wait is inserted only before subsequent rounds.\n    -   `--wait` without a value retains the existing interactive behavior — waits for user confirmation before each prompt.\n    -   No flag (or `--no-wait`) means no waiting, which is now the default. `--no-wait` is kept for backward compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed `CliAgent` failing with `Missing --harness in non-dry run mode` when no `harness` is provided: `CliAgent` now falls back to the `PTBK_HARNESS` environment variable, mirroring `ptbk agent exec` behavior. Similarly falls back to `PTBK_MODEL` and `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL` env vars. Extracted shared env-var constants (`PTBK_HARNESS_ENV`, `PTBK_MODEL_ENV`, `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL_ENV`), harness names (`CLI_AGENT_HARNESS_NAMES`), and thinking-level values (`CLI_AGENT_THINKING_LEVEL_VALUES`) into the new `src/book-3.0/cliAgentEnv.ts` so CLI and library share a single source of truth. Fixed a pre-existing TypeScript error in `BookNodeAgentSource.ts` where `normalizeBookNodeAgentSource` did not accept the plain `string` allowed by its `book` option type.\n\n-   Fixed entity scanner false positive in `agentProjectPaths.ts` where the comment `// Re-export shared agent folder path constants...` caused the regex to match `export shared agent` and flag a missing `@private`/`@public` annotation; removed the misleading comment.\n\n-   Fixed `@promptbook/node` bundle so CLI-only `[🟡]` path constants no longer leak into the package: extracted shared agent-folder path constants (`AGENT_BOOK_FILE_PATH`, `AGENT_MESSAGES_DIRECTORY_PATH`, `AGENT_QUEUED_MESSAGES_DIRECTORY_PATH`, `AGENT_FINISHED_MESSAGES_DIRECTORY_PATH`, `AGENT_FAILED_MESSAGES_DIRECTORY_PATH`, `AGENT_PROJECTS_DIRECTORY_PATH`) into `src/book-3.0/agentFolderPaths.ts`, updated `agentProjectPaths.ts` to import and re-export from there, and updated `executeAgentChatTurn.ts` plus both agent-message prompt builders to import from the shared file instead of the CLI-only one. Added `[💞]` ignore note to `agentFolderPaths.ts` to suppress the file-name/entity-name discrepancy check.\n\n-   Optimized `CliAgent` to call the agent execution pipeline directly instead of spawning a `ptbk agent exec` child process, removing the intermediate CLI overhead while sharing the same `executeAgentChatTurn` logic used by the CLI command.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server chat pre-answers so the immediate placeholder response now focuses on confirming the job is being handled and avoids partial deliverables such as draft code or likely final-answer content.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server work during chat detail loads, and adding active chat job/timeout indexes for the hottest polling queries.\n\n-   Changed `ptbk agent chat` and `ptbk agent exec` console output so local harness error-report tests so they assert the current Promptbook and Book version constants instead of stale hard-coded prerelease values.\n\n-   Added `CliAgent` and `LiteAgent` to `@promptbook/node` for   Added regression coverage for the commitment ordering in the shared catalog, the documentation dropdown, and Monaco completion suggestions.\n\n-   Added built-in TEAM hierarchy support to Agents Server transpiled-code exports, so exported harnesses now include teammate metadata and sources instead of depending on a running Agents Server for `TEAM` tools:\n\n    -
