as before.\n    -   Tool calling works as before.\n    -   Caching of the agents and underlying assistants works as before.\n    -   It works in the `Agents Server` application `/apps/agents-server`.\n    -   All existing features work as before.\n    -   Kept `OpenAiAssistantExecutionTools`, marked as deprecated and not used in `Agent`.\n-   Fixed document preview and download in Agents Server chat:\n    -   Resolved issue where source URLs with query parameters (e.g. from blob storage) were not matched correctly, preventing previews.\n    -   Fixed download button for cross-origin files by implementing a fetch-and-download mechanism to bypass browser restrictions on `download` attribute.\n-   Improve the chat UI responsiveness by allowing user interaction (sending messages) while waiting for the agent reply.\n-   Fixed tool-call chip styling so the chips keep their natural casing/spacing while the tool-call modal uses a dedicated `toolCallModalLabel`, keeping both places readable.\n-   Fixed document preview modal for KNOWLEDGE sources in Agents Server chat:\n    -   Resolved issue where document preview was showing \"Agent Not Found\" error due to invalid URL resolution\n    -   Fixed preview to only load when a valid URL is available (checks for http:// or https://)\n    -   Removed technical clutter (Citation ID, Source, URL fields) from the modal for a cleaner user experience\n    -   Redesigned download button with modern styling matching the application's design system\n    -   Added proper error handling when preview is unavailable, showing a user-friendly message\n    -   Simplified modal header to show only document name (without file extension) for better readability\n-   Fixed image generation caching to consider all generation parameters (model, size, quality, style) in the cache key, ensuring that changing these parameters generates a new image instead of returning a cached one from a previous generation with different settings.\n-   Fixed image generation caching to include input images (attachments) in the cache key, ensuring that using the same prompt with different input images generates new results.\n-   Improved self-learning experience in `Agent` class:\n    -   The agent now returns the generated answer immediately before starting the self-learning process.\n    -   Self-learning is performed asynchronously in the background.\n    -   A \"Self learning\" chip is displayed during the learning phase, similar to tool usage chips.\n    -   This enhances user experience by eliminating the wait time for self-learning completion.\n-   Enhanced codebase by using explicit types instead of type inference across multiple files in `src/`, `apps/`, and `scripts/` directories to improve readability and maintainability.\n-   Fix width of the message in the chat by adding a minimum width and improving layout for short messages.\n-   Use model `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` for the agent of Avatar Images\n-   Updated `openai` from `4.63.0` to `6.18.0` and fixed all resulting type errors.\n-   Resolved `zod` peer dependency conflicts between `@ai-sdk/deepseek` and `@openai/agents` by using `overrides` in `package.json`.\n-   Fixed `node-fetch` declaration issue in `LindatAutomaticTranslator.ts` by using native `URLSearchParams` and removing `node-fetch` import.\n-   Stabilized Agents Server under low traffic by removing constant 5-second DB polling from timeout/preparation workers, restoring durable timeout wake-ups through Vercel cron, fixing agent-source cycle detection across canonical/name URLs, and reducing agent-reference resolver churn.\n-   Logged richer durable diagnostics for failed Agents Server chat turns so admin task inspection no longer stops at the generic lease-expired summary:\n\n    -   Added backwards-compatible `failureDetails` storage for `UserChatJob` rows and now persist structured JSON diagnostics containing the failure summary, serialized error payload (message/name/stack when available), provider, timing, and chat-turn identifiers.\n    -   Reused the same diagnostics builder for runtime failures, unexpected worker-route failures, and expired-lease recovery paths to keep failure logging DRY and consistent.\n    -   Extended the admin task manager to surface the stored diagnostics under failed chat-completion tasks via an expandable \"Show details\" panel in the Last error column.\n\n-   Refactored Agents Server `apps/agents-server/src/app/agents/[agentName]/api/chat/route.ts` into smaller focused private chat-route helpers without changing external behavior:\n\n    -   Moved request-time runtime assembly, disclaimer and credential resolution, history initialization, and frozen team-member chat persistence behind the private `resolveAgentChatRouteContext` and `createTeamMemberFrozenChatPersistence` facades so `route.ts` now reads as a thin HTTP entrypoint.\n    -   Extracted the long-lived markdown stream orchestration, cancellation handling, tool-call framing, and final post-processing into the private `createAgentChatStreamResponse` helper while preserving the existing stateless chat streaming behavior, keep-alives, history recording, learning, and calendar activity logging.\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server new-agent wizard team step so it now behaves as a homepage-style multi-select picker:\n\n    -   Removed the separate manual \"Team members\" entry UI and kept only the existing-agents picker headed by \"Browse existing agents\" / \"Vyberte existující agenty\".\n    -   Kept multi-selection for teammate agents across the local server and federated servers while continuing to exclude the hidden core server from federated lists.\n    -   Extracted a shared homepage-like `AgentCardsSection` renderer so the wizard and federated-agent surfaces reuse the same card-grid, loading, empty, and error presentation.\n\n-   Improved Agents Server expired chat-worker diagnostics so the stale \"Background worker lease expired before the chat turn finished.\" failure now leaves actionable evidence instead of a generic summary:\n\n    -   Added shared expired-lease diagnostics for durable chat jobs that record queue/run/heartbeat timing, worker runtime thresholds, configured server limits, and a snapshot of active chat jobs and timeouts at the moment recovery runs.\n    -   Started logging structured `lease_expired` recovery/reconciliation events so server logs show which background tasks were active and whether the job had already outlived the 300-second worker route limit when heartbeats stopped.\n\n-   Added immediate optimistic profile-to-chat navigation in Agents Server, so starting a first message from an agent profile now swaps to the chat route without waiting for the server and keeps the user bubble visible throughout the handoff:\n\n    -   Persisted profile-to-chat optimistic turn metadata across the route transition, including the client message id reused later for canonical reconciliation and failure states.\n    -   Added a chat-route loading surface that renders the pending user turn right away while the standalone chat page server data is still loading.\n    -   Tightened optimistic/canonical merge ordering so unresolved user bubbles stay ahead of later assistant streaming messages until the server confirms them.\n\n-   Added the new deterministic `AsciiOctopus` avatar visual alongside the existing avatar set, with an animated ASCII-art rendering that keeps the same organic alien octopus feel as `Octopus3` while varying its blob silhouette, tentacle count, face, and colors from the agent name, hash, colors, and animation time:\n\n    -   Added the new built-in `ascii-octopus` canvas renderer to the shared avatar registry without changing the existing `Octopus`, `Octopus2`, `Octopus3`, pixel-art, Minecraft, or Fractal visuals.\n    -   Kept the implementation DRY by reusing shared octopus body and tentacle geometry helpers, while translating that geometry into deterministic ASCII glyphs instead of painted surfaces.\n    -   Updated the existing utils `/avatars` playground and regression coverage so the new renderer appears in the selector, preview grid, deterministic sample gallery, and supported URL-state parsing without creating a separate page.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server metadata enum handling so predefined metadata keys no longer accept arbitrary strings in `/admin/metadata`:\n\n    -   Added shared metadata definitions with reusable predefined option lists, so enum-like metadata such as `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL`, `SERVER_LANGUAGE`, `SERVER_VISIBILITY`, `CHAT_FEEDBACK_MODE`, `CHAT_VISUAL_MODE`, `NAME_POOL`, `DEFAULT_VISIBILITY`, and `NEW_AGENT_WIZARD` now render as selects instead of free-form text inputs.\n    -   Reused the same option registries across the metadata page and existing server-creation flows to keep enum values centralized and DRY.\n    -   Added server-side validation for predefined metadata options, so invalid enum values are rejected even when `/api/metadata` is called directly.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk agent-folder run` / `ptbk agent-folder tick` with the GitHub Copilot runner on Windows/MSYS for large queued-message prompts:\n\n    -   Stopped passing the full generated agent prompt as one `copilot -p \"...\"` shell argument, which could exceed the shell/Node argument-length limit and fail with `Argument list too long`.\n    -   Switched the GitHub Copilot runner to feed prompts through standard input instead, keeping `--model`, `--reasoning-effort`, and the existing non-interactive flags unchanged.\n    -   Added regression coverage for the new stdin-based invocation shape so agent-mode prompts stay safe even when the Book Language blueprint makes them much larger than coder prompts.\n\n-   Enhanced the `ptbk agent-folder run` rich terminal UI so it now reflects queued-message workflows instead of mirroring `ptbk coder run`:\n\n    -   The top branding now uses compact initials derived from the local `agent.book` title, making the dashboard identify the actual agent definition rather than only the runner selected by `--harness`.\n    -   The session summary now distinguishes the local agent from the execution runner and shows queue-specific totals (`finished` / `queued` / total) with a progress bar based on answered messages instead of `Task 1/1`.\n    -   Added a dedicated `User message` box that shows the latest `MESSAGE @User` block 1:1 with line-preserving trimming, while keeping the live streaming output panel unchanged.\n\n-   Enhanced the `ptbk agent-folder run` terminal dashboard so long-running agent sessions stay inside one stable rich UI:\n\n    -   Kept a single persistent boxed UI alive across queued-message runs, moving idle watching and idle auto-pull activity into explicit in-frame `WAITING` / loading states instead of printing plain lines that broke the layout mid-session.\n    -   Changed the header visual to render the local agent name in a smaller compact banner instead of large initials, while keeping the rest of the terminal frame layout intact.\n    -   Kept the queued-thread preview focused on the latest `MESSAGE @User` from the `.book` thread via `src/book-3.0/Book.ts`, and deferred the coding-agent Git identity tip until process exit so it no longer interrupts active sessions or `--no-ui` streaming output.\n\n-   Refactored `OpenAiAssistantExecutionTools` internals to keep OpenAI Assistants behavior unchanged while making the module easier to follow and maintain:\n\n    -   Split `src/llm-providers/openai/OpenAiAssistantExecutionTools.ts` into a smaller orchestration facade plus focused private helpers for prompt/thread building, tool-run execution, streaming/result reporting, and citation rewriting.\n    -   Kept assistant chat execution, tool progress streaming, hosted tool invocation, file attachment handling, assistant creation/update flows, and final Promptbook result export behavior unchanged while reducing the responsibility count inside the top-level file.\n\n-   Fixed the self-contained Stalwart mail server of Agents Server, which rejected every management call and therefore never routed inbound or outbound agent mail:\n\n    -   Fixed `install.sh`, which decided that Stalwart was already bootstrapped whenever `/etc/stalwart/config.json` existed. Stalwart writes that file itself - it is only its storage descriptor, for example `{\"@type\":\"RocksDb\",\"path\":\"/var/lib/stalwart/\",...}` - already during its very first startup, long before anything is bootstrapped, and never touches it again. The installer therefore skipped the `x:Bootstrap/set` call on **every** fresh installation and left the mail server permanently in bootstrap mode, where it refuses every management call with `{\"type\":\"forbidden\",\"description\":\"The server is in bootstrap mode. ...\"}`. The bootstrap state is now read from Stalwart itself through a management probe, so a pending bootstrap is completed on the next installer run and an already bootstrapped server is left untouched.\n    -   Fixed the Stalwart management payloads, which sent JSON arrays for `aliases`, `credentials`, `memberGroupIds`, `stages`, and the MTA hook `enable.match` expression, while Stalwart serializes every `set` / `objectList` property as an object and answered `invalidPatch` / `Invalid value for object property`. Added shared `toStalwartJmapSet` and `toStalwartJmapObjectList` helpers so all payloads build these shapes in one place.\n    -   Fixed `install.sh`, which provisioned the Agents Server Stalwart administrator inside the reserved `promptbook.invalid` domain. Stalwart rejects such a domain as an `Invalid domain name`, so the step failed and, because of `set -Eeuo pipefail`, aborted the whole installation before nginx, firewall, and certificate configuration ever ran. The bootstrap-time administrator credentials are now kept as Stalwart's fixed `STALWART_RECOVERY_ADMIN` credentials instead of provisioning a second administrator account.\n    -   Fixed the Stalwart step of `install.sh` aborting the whole installation when the mail server cannot be bootstrapped. Because `configure_firewall`, `configure_nginx_reverse_proxy`, and `configure_ssl_certificates` all run afterwards, a mail server problem used to leave the VPS without a firewall, reverse proxy, or certificates. The step now warns and continues, and the bootstrap is retried by every later installer run.\n    -   Fixed outbound submission, which was configured for port `587`, a port a bootstrapped Stalwart never opens. Agents Server now submits through `submissions` on port `465` with implicit TLS, and the email server administration pages document that port instead of `587`.\n    -   Fixed the catch-all address being assigned before the mailbox behind it existed, so synchronizing an already-known domain no longer fails on its first management call.\n    -   Improved Stalwart error reporting so a rejected object now includes Stalwart's own `notCreated` / `notUpdated` reason, and a server still in **bootstrap mode** reports an actionable message instead of a raw `forbidden` response.\n    -   Fixed the `promptbook-agents-server` build, which loaded the Next.js command line interface through the hardcoded path `../../node_modules/next/dist/bin/next`. That path does not exist inside a git worktree without its own installed dependencies, such as the `ptbk coder --isolate` worktrees, so `npm run build` failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` even though Next.js was resolvable. The new `apps/agents-server/scripts/next-cli.js` resolves it through Node's own module resolution instead.\n\n-   Fixed the self-contained Stalwart mail server staying unusable whenever its initial setup was left pending. Completing that setup used to be the sole responsibility of `install.sh`, so a mail server which was installed before the bootstrap fix - or whose bootstrap failed once - answered every management call with `{\"type\":\"forbidden\",\"description\":\"The server is in bootstrap mode. ...\"}`, and **Synchronize Stalwart** on `/admin/email-server` could only report the error, never resolve it. Because the VPS self-update runs the _deployed_ release's installer, such a server stayed broken for at least one more update cycle. Agents Server now completes the bootstrap itself as the first step of every domain synchronization, which happens on startup and on **Synchronize Stalwart**, and it asks Stalwart for its bootstrap state instead of inferring it from files on disk. The setup Stalwart receives - mail hostname, default domain, automatic DKIM keys, and no ACME certificate request because nginx and certbot own every certificate on the VPS - is now defined by `buildStalwartBootstrapValue`, which `install.sh` mirrors under the shared `[📬]` marker because a fresh VPS is bootstrapped before Agents Server is built, and the result is verified against Stalwart itself so a bootstrap that was accepted but not applied is reported with the remaining manual step instead of a raw `forbidden` response. The installer keeps performing the bootstrap for a fresh installation and additionally waits until Stalwart really left bootstrap mode after the restart it needs to open its mail listeners, so the first synchronization of a newly started Agents Server no longer races a mail server that is still coming up.\n-   Improved the Agents Server **Book language manual** so its linked table of contents navigates directly to each commitment, and each end-to-end example links its used commitments back to their sections. The manual now describes `@Foo` and `{Foo foo}` as agent references rather than parameters, renames the `---` primitive to **Multiple agent**, documents code fences as ` ``` `, links every generated-from source to the Promptbook repository, hides parser/runtime implementation details and unfinished commitments, and keeps each commitment example focused on its canonical keyword with only `GOAL` and `CLOSED` as supporting syntax.\n\n-   Fixed the published `@promptbook/components` package, which broke the production build of every browser application that installs `ptbk`, `promptbook` or `@promptbook/components`. Rendered markdown is sanitized by `DOMPurify`, which needs a DOM, so `renderMarkdown` creates one through `jsdom` whenever it runs outside of a browser - for example during server-side rendering. That code path is unreachable in a browser, but bundlers resolve `require('jsdom')` statically, so `next build` followed it into `jsdom` and failed with **Module not found: Can't resolve `fs`** together with the same error for `child_process` and `net`. It failed even for an application that imports `<MarkdownContent/>` with `ssr: false`, because a bundler resolves a module it will never execute just as eagerly as one it will:\n\n    -   The generated manifest of every package that is not Node-only now declares `\"browser\": { \"jsdom\": false }`, which is the standard way to tell a browser bundler to replace a Node-only dependency with an empty module. Browser builds therefore no longer follow `jsdom` (and no longer ship it), while Node.js ignores the `browser` field and keeps resolving the real library for server-side rendering. The stubs are derived from the dependencies which the generated package really has, so a Node-only dependency which appears in a browser-facing package in the future is covered without another manual change.\n    -   Creating the server-side DOM moved from `renderMarkdown` into `$provideServerDomWindow`, which is now the single place where browser-facing code touches `jsdom`. A runtime that can provide neither the DOM of a browser nor `jsdom` is now reported as a branded `EnvironmentMismatchError` explaining why markdown can not be sanitized, instead of failing with `JSDOM is not a constructor`.\n    -   The list of Node-only packages is now shared through `isNodeOnlyPackage` between the publish-safety check and the dependency step of the package generation, instead of being written down twice.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":3,"newStart":1,"newLines":17,"lines":["+-   Made the subscription usage shown by `ptbk coder run` live. The **Usage** rows of the terminal dashboard used to be","+    read once before the queue started and then once more after each finished prompt, so for the whole round — which can","+    easily be hours — they described a moment that had already passed. They are now re-read every 5 seconds by one shared","+    refresher which the run starts once and stops when it ends, so the remaining percentages and the reset countdowns","+    always describe the present moment instead of the state the harness was in when the current prompt started. Two","+    reads never overlap: a tick which arrives while the previous read is still in flight is skipped, so a slow or","+    hanging harness cannot pile requests up, and a harness without subscription limits or a run without the dashboard","+    starts no timer at all. OpenAI Codex already answers every single read with a fresh account snapshot, while Claude","+    Code reports its limits as events of the stream it is writing — so the Claude Code runner now reads its limits from","+    the live output as well, instead of only from the finished one, which is what gives the 5-second refresh something","+    new to show in the middle of a prompt. To make that possible, every script runner can now observe completed output","+    lines while the script is still running, and the buffering which turns arbitrarily chopped chunks into whole lines","+    is shared by both of them. The `ptbk coder` landing page documents the new refresh.","+"," -   Fixed the warnings printed while installing `ptbk`. Five of the ten `npm warn deprecated` lines were caused by","     Promptbook itself and are gone, and an installation resolves 96 packages fewer than before:"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cf9L7fiSapunvW3FdTXQu","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'll wait for the verification suite to finish. While it runs, here's what I found and changed:\n\n## Analysis of the current behaviour\n\nThe Usage rows in the `ptbk coder run` dashboard come from `HarnessSubscriptionUsage` and were read at exactly two moments:\n\n- `runCodexPrompts.ts:139` — once, before the queue starts\n- `runPromptRound.ts:165` — once, after each prompt finishes\n\nSo for the entire round (often hours) the percentages and reset countdowns described a moment that had already passed. Per harness:\n\n- **OpenAI Codex** — `getCodexSubscriptionUsage` queries the local `codex app-server` over JSON-RPC, so every call is genuinely fresh; it was simply never called mid-prompt.\n- **Claude Code** — reports limits as `rate_limit_event` entries in its stream, but `ClaudeCodeRunner` parsed them only from the *finished* output, so polling it would have returned last prompt's numbers.\n\n## Changes\n\n**One shared refresher** — `scripts/run-codex-prompts/ui/startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh.ts` reuses the existing `refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage` on a 5 s interval. Reads never overlap (a tick during an in-flight read is skipped), the timer is `unref`'d, and no timer starts at all for a harness without subscription limits or a run without a dashboard. `runCodexPrompts` starts it once and stops it in its `finally`; the per-prompt refresh in `runPromptRound` is gone, so there is now one place that keeps the usage current.\n\n**Claude Code reads its limits live** — `RunGoScriptOptions` gained `onOutputLine`, honoured by both script runners, and `ClaudeCodeRunner` feeds rate-limit lines into its snapshot while the prompt is still running. Lines are recognised by type before anything is parsed, so the far more frequent tool/message lines cost nothing. The chunk→line buffering is now one shared `createScriptOutputLineReader`, which also replaced the duplicated stdout/stderr buffer logic in `runScriptUntilMarkerIdle`.\n\n**Docs** — landing page `advancedFeatures.ts` + its spec now state the 5-second re-read; changelog entry added at the top of `_current-preversion.md`.\n\nTargeted tests pass (28 suites, 131 tests across `runGoScript`, `main` and `runners`), `tsc` is clean at the repo root and in `apps/coder-landing`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":244,"cache_read_input_tokens":196001,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":244},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"74608ceb-c452-4e82-b385-4ad6b325ff5b","uuid":"dbc53edb-e88f-47ba-bc65-64459f2b5338","timestamp":"2026-09-17T16:30:58.097Z","request_id":"req_011Cf9L7fEBH53bCDR7EfThF"}

### Emoji in `[brackets]`

-   `[number]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the file

-   `[🚉]` Marks an types / interfaces / structures fully serializable as JSON, not marking `string_` and `number_` prefixed aliases
-   `[🧹]` Need to implement garbage collection
-   `[🐣]` Easter eggs
-   `[💩]` Shitty code that needs refactoring
-   `$` When entity (function, class) starts by `$`, it means it is not pure and can have side effects.
-   3x `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed before releasing a pre-release version.
-   4x (and more) `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed as soon as possible.
-   `@@@` Marks a place where text / documentation / ... must be written.

### Dictionary

-   **Promptbook Engine vs. Agent Server** sre two distinct parts you should know the difference:
    -   **Promptbook Engine** is the core engine that powers AI agents, it is located in `/src` folder. It is framework-agnostic and can be used in different applications. It can run as standalone javascript/typescript library, CLI environment, or be integrated into different applications. It can be also runned in Agent Server:
    -   **Agent Server** is a specific application that uses the Promptbook Engine to provide a web and API interface for creating and interacting with AI agents. It is located in `/apps/agents-server` folder.
-   **Commitments** are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents
    -   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, etc.
    -   Commitments are in the folder `/src/commitments`
    -   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g., `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a begining of the line and end by new co
    -   Agent source with commitments is parsed by two functions:
        -   `parseAgentSource` which is a lightweight parser for agent source, it parses basic information and its purpose is to be quick and synchronous. The commitments there are hardcoded.
        -   `createAgentModelRequirements` which is an asynchronous function that creates model requirements it applies each commitment one by one and works asynchronously.

-   Always analyze the context and requirements before generating any code.

    -   If you don't know, prefer to mark it as private, we can always change it to public later, but changing from public to private may cause breaking changes.

#### Agents server installed on VPS _(as additional context)_

-   There are two distinct things:
    1. Entire VPS
    2. Each server
-   On one VPS there can be multiple servers and each server has its own domain
-   Most things (like agents, projects, metadata, etc.) are living on each server and some things (like environment variables, superadmin, etc.) are bound to entire VPS
-   Purpose of this is to be able to run multiple clients on one VPS and each client can have its own server with its own domain and settings
-   The entire VPS is managed by superadmin and each server is managed by normal admin of that server _(or superadmin can also manage each server)_
-   Superadmin has always name `admin` and password hardcoded in environment variable `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
-   The VPS is installed by running [the `install.sh`](install.sh) script on a fresh VPS
-   Servers can be added and removed by superadmin on `/superadmin/servers` page

#### The Agents Server menu _(as additional context)_

The menu of the agent server looks like this:

1. The navigation hierarchy
    - Icon and Server name _(for example Promptbook Agents Server)_
    - arrow ">" and Agents or picked agent name (organized in folders)
    - arrow ">" and the view Profile / Chat / Book of the agent or nothing if no agent is picked
2. The menu items
    - Documentation
    - System
3. Control panel and user menu
    - Control panel
    - User menu with the avatar and the name of the user

#### Database migrations for Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   Migrations are located in `apps/agents-server/src/database/migrations`
-   Be aware that table names in migrations have prefix `prefix_` _(look at existing migrations for reference)_
-   Migrations should be backwards compatible:
    -   Meaning that earlier versions of the server should be able to run with the database after migration without any issues.
    -   This is important because we want to have the same database for production and preview environments.
    -   This database will be migrated to the latest version of the preview environment, but the production environment should be able to run with it without any issues.
    -   The only thing that can happen is that older versions of the server will not be able to use new features.
    -   Adding new columns, tables, etc. is fine, but do not remove or rename existing ones, and do not change the meaning of existing columns or tables.
    -   When in doubt, prefer to add new things instead of changing existing ones.

#### Metadata of Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   There is a table called `Metadata`.
-   It has `key` and `value` fields.
-   It is a similar concept to configuration, but this configuration can be changed by administrators in the Agents Server website.

#### Book Language blueprint _(as additional context)_

Book language is a domain-specific language used for defining AI agents in the Promptbook Engine and Agents server.
It has lightweight syntax and keywords (the commitments) that allow you to define the "soul" of the agent.
The book language is designed to be human-readable and easy to write, while also being powerful enough to express complex agent behaviors.

Every agent has its source defined in the book language, which is called "agent source". The agent source is parsed and processed by the Promptbook Engine to create the actual AI agent that can interact with users and perform tasks.
This agent source is internally converted to a structured format called "agent model requirements" which are the actual raw technical instructions for the AI model to run the agent.

There is a standalone book language documentation on each agent server on `/api/docs/book.md` route, for example `https://live.ptbk.io/api/docs/book-language.md?language=en`.
Use it as a reference for the syntax and semantics of the book language, and modify `apps/agents-server/src/utils/bookLanguageDocumentation/createStandaloneBookLanguageMarkdown.ts` if it is relevant to the change you are doing.

##### Commitments _(as additional context and part of Book Language)_

Commitments are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents written in `book` language.

-   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, `CLOSED`, etc.
-   They are in the folder `src/commitments`.
-   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g. `PERSONA`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a beginning of the line and ends by a new commitment or the end of the book.
-   There is a general pattern that the commitment keyword is followed by a space and then by the content of the commitment, for example:
    -   `PERSONA You are a helpful assistant that helps with cooking recipes.`
    -   `USE MCP https://mcp.example.com/server`
-   In the commitment context, you can reference external agents, for example:
    -   `TEAM You can talk to {Criminal lawyer} and {Financial advisor}`

const CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 5 * 1000;\n\n/**\n * Stops the periodic subscription-usage refresh of one coder run.\n *\n * @private internal type of coder run UI\n */\nexport type CoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefreshHandle = {\n    /**\n     * Ends the refresh, after which the dashboard keeps the last read values.\n     */\n    stop(): void;\n};\n\n/**\n * Keeps the harness subscription usage of the coder-run dashboard current for the whole run.\n *\n * A single coding prompt can take hours, so reading the usage once per prompt leaves the dashboard showing values\n * which are long out of date. Reading it on its own clock instead means the percentages and reset countdowns always\n * describe the present moment, no matter how long the current prompt runs.\n *\n * Refreshes never overlap: a read which is still in flight when the next tick arrives simply skips that tick, so a\n * slow or hanging harness cannot pile up requests. The whole refresh is optional dashboard information, so a harness\n * without subscription limits and a run without a dashboard start no timer at all.\n *\n * @private internal utility of coder run UI\n */\nexport function startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh(options: {\n    readonly runner: PromptRunner;\n    readonly uiState: CoderRunUiState | undefined;\n    readonly refreshIntervalMs?: number;\n}): CoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefreshHandle {\n    const { runner, uiState, refreshIntervalMs = CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS } = options;\n\n    if (!uiState || !runner.getSubscriptionUsage) {\n        return { stop: () => {} };\n    }\n\n    let isRefreshing = false;\n\n    /**\n     * Reads one fresh snapshot unless the previous read has not finished yet.\n     */\n    const refreshSubscriptionUsage = (): void => {\n        if (isRefreshing) {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        isRefreshing = true;\n        void refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage({ runner, uiState }).finally(() => {\n            isRefreshing = false;\n        });\n    };\n\n    // Note: The dashboard shows the usage from its very first frames on instead of waiting out one whole interval\n    refreshSubscriptionUsage();\n\n    const refreshInterval = setInterval(refreshSubscriptionUsage, refreshIntervalMs);\n\n    // Note: Optional dashboard information must never keep the `ptbk coder` process alive after the queue is done\n    refreshInterval.unref?.();\n\n    return {\n        stop(): void {\n            clearInterval(refreshInterval);\n        },\n    };\n}\n","numLines":78,"startLine":1,"totalLines":78}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FZr1C9RX6fXimrDxzSBdbU","type":"tool_result","content":"commit d6cd92c16c0e92466ac71a25f613b118f6620db0\nAuthor: Pavol Hejny <me@pavolhejny.com>\nDate:   Thu Sep 17 18:52:39 2026 +0200\n\n    [✨🍔] Show the usage of `ptbk coder` in real-time not freezed on each prompt\n    \n    -   Refresh the usage percentages each 5s\n    -   Keep in mind the DRY _(don't repeat yourself)_ principle.\n    -   Do a proper analysis of the current functionality of `ptbk coder` and related functionality before you start implementing.\n    -   You are working with [`ptbk coder`](src/cli/cli-commands/coder/run.ts)\n    -   Update the [`ptbk coder` landing website](apps/coder-landing) if there are any changes that affect the landing page.\n    -   Add the changes into the [changelog](changelog/_current-preversion.md)\n\ndiff --git a/changelog/_current-preversion.md b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\nindex b6f9983b3..40fec2718 100644\n--- a/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n+++ b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n@@ -1,3 +1,17 @@\n+-   Made the subscription usage shown by `ptbk coder run` live. The **Usage** rows of the terminal dashboard used to be\n+    read once before the queue started and then once more after each finished prompt, so for the whole round — which can\n+    easily be hours — they described a moment that had already passed. They are now re-read every 5 seconds by one shared\n+    refresher which the run starts once and stops when it ends, so the remaining percentages and the reset countdowns\n+    always describe the present moment instead of the state the harness was in when the current prompt started. Two\n+    reads never overlap: a tick which arrives while the previous read is still in flight is skipped, so a slow or\n+    hanging harness cannot pile requests up, and a harness without subscription limits or a run without the dashboard\n+    starts no timer at all. OpenAI Codex already answers every single read with a fresh account snapshot, while Claude\n+    Code reports its limits as events of the stream it is writing — so the Claude Code runner now reads its limits from\n+    the live output as well, instead of only from the finished one, which is what gives the 5-second refresh something\n+    new to show in the middle of a prompt. To make that possible, every script runner can now observe completed output\n+    lines while the script is still running, and the buffering which turns arbitrarily chopped chunks into whole lines\n+    is shared by both of them. The `ptbk coder` landing page documents the new refresh.\n+\n -   Fixed the warnings printed while installing `ptbk`. Five of the ten `npm warn deprecated` lines were caused by\n     Promptbook itself and are gone, and an installation resolves 96 packages fewer than before:","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"16bbd1a0-fdb9-4301-b22a-bed2255d0f09","uuid":"3913b83a-a052-487f-bcd3-7bc781bc48b8","timestamp":"2026-09-17T17:03:56.480Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"commit d6cd92c16c0e92466ac71a25f613b118f6620db0\nAuthor: Pavol Hejny <me@pavolhejny.com>\nDate:   Thu Sep 17 18:52:39 2026 +0200\n\n    [✨🍔] Show the usage of `ptbk coder` in real-time not freezed on each prompt\n    \n    -   Refresh the usage percentages each 5s\n    -   Keep in mind the DRY _(don't repeat yourself)_ principle.\n    -   Do a proper analysis of the current functionality of `ptbk coder` and related functionality before you start implementing.\n    -   You are working with [`ptbk coder`](src/cli/cli-commands/coder/run.ts)\n    -   Update the [`ptbk coder` landing website](apps/coder-landing) if there are any changes that affect the landing page.\n    -   Add the changes into the [changelog](changelog/_current-preversion.md)\n\ndiff --git a/changelog/_current-preversion.md b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\nindex b6f9983b3..40fec2718 100644\n--- a/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n+++ b/changelog/_current-preversion.md\n@@ -1,3 +1,17 @@\n+-   Made the subscription usage shown by `ptbk coder run` live. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017Mo9e7w9drMn1j4x6AYNSo","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport colors from 'colors';\n2\timport { formatDurationMs } from '../common/parseDuration';\n3\timport type { HarnessSubscriptionUsage } from '../runners/types/HarnessSubscriptionUsage';\n4\timport type { SessionRow } from './buildRunUiFrameShared';\n5\t\n6\t/**\n7\t * Label shown on the first subscription-usage row in the terminal Session box.\n8\t */\n9\tconst SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_SESSION_LABEL = 'Usage';\n10\t\n11\t/**\n12\t * Number of milliseconds in one calendar-free day used for compact reset countdowns.\n13\t */\n14\tconst ONE_DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n15\t\n16\t/**\n17\t * Builds every available subscription-limit row for the terminal Session box.\n18\t *\n19\t * The first row carries the `Usage` label and subsequent rows stay aligned beneath it, allowing a harness to report\n20\t * any number of windows instead of making the dashboard assume a fixed 5-hour/weekly pair.\n21\t *\n22\t * @private internal utility of coder run UI\n23\t */\n24\texport function buildSubscriptionUsageSessionRows(\n25\t    subscriptionUsage: HarnessSubscriptionUsage | undefined,\n26\t    currentTimeMs = Date.now(),\n27\t): readonly SessionRow[] {\n28\t    if (!subscriptionUsage || subscriptionUsage.limits.length === 0) {\n29\t        return [];\n30\t    }\n31\t\n32\t    return subscriptionUsage.limits.map((limit, index) => ({\n33\t        label: index === 0 ? SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_SESSION_LABEL : '',\n34\t        value: formatSubscriptionUsageLimit(limit, currentTimeMs),\n35\t    }));\n36\t}\n37\t\n38\t/**\n39\t * Formats one remaining subscription limit and its optional reset time for the terminal dashboard.\n40\t *\n41\t * @private helper of `buildSubscriptionUsageSessionRows`\n42\t */\n43\tfunction formatSubscriptionUsageLimit(\n44\t    limit: HarnessSubscriptionUsage['limits'][number],\n45\t    currentTimeMs: number,\n46\t): string {\n47\t    const remainingPercentage = Math.round(Math.max(0, Math.min(100, 100 - limit.usedPercentage)));\n48\t    const remainingPercentageColor = resolveRemainingPercentageColor(remainingPercentage);\n49\t    const resetText = formatSubscriptionUsageReset(limit.resetsAt, currentTimeMs);\n50\t    const label = limit.label.trim() || SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_SESSION_LABEL;\n51\t\n52\t    return [\n53\t        colors.bold(label),\n54\t        remainingPercentageColor(`${remainingPercentage}% remaining`),\n55\t        ...(resetText ? [colors.gray(resetText)] : []),\n56\t    ].join('  ·  ');\n57\t}\n58\t\n59\t/**\n60\t * Chooses an attention color for the remaining subscription percentage.\n61\t *\n62\t * @private helper of `buildSubscriptionUsageSessionRows`\n63\t */\n64\tfunction resolveRemainingPercentageColor(remainingPercentage: number): (text: string) => string {\n65\t    if (remainingPercentage === 0) {\n66\t        return colors.red;\n67\t    }\n68\t\n69\t    if (remainingPercentage <= 20) {\n70\t        return colors.yellow;\n71\t    }\n72\t\n73\t    return colors.green;\n74\t}\n75\t\n76\t/**\n77\t * Formats the optional future reset timestamp of one subscription limit.\n78\t *\n79\t * @private helper of `buildSubscriptionUsageSessionRows`\n80\t */\n81\tfunction formatSubscriptionUsageReset(resetsAt: number | undefined, currentTimeMs: number): string | undefined {\n82\t    if (resetsAt === undefined) {\n83\t        return undefined;\n84\t    }\n85\t\n86\t    const remainingDurationMs = resetsAt * 1000 - currentTimeMs;\n87\t\n88\t    if (remainingDurationMs <= 0) {\n89\t        return 'resets now';\n90\t    }\n91\t\n92\t    return `resets in ${formatSubscriptionUsageDuration(remainingDurationMs)}`;\n93\t}\n94\t\n95\t/**\n96\t * Formats a reset countdown with days when a weekly-style limit is still several days away.\n97\t *\n98\t * @private helper of `buildSubscriptionUsageSessionRows`\n99\t */\n100\tfunction formatSubscriptionUsageDuration(durationMs: number): string {\n101\t    const dayCount = Math.floor(durationMs / ONE_DAY_MS);\n102\t\n103\t    if (dayCount === 0) {\n104\t        return formatDurationMs(durationMs);\n105\t    }\n106\t\n107\t    const remainingDurationMs = durationMs - dayCount * ONE_DAY_MS;\n108\t\n109\t    return remainingDurationMs === 0 ? SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_SESSION_LABEL : '',\n        value: formatSubscriptionUsageLimit(limit, currentTimeMs),\n    }));\n}\n\n/**\n * Formats one remaining subscription limit and its optional reset time for the terminal dashboard.\n *\n * @private helper of `buildSubscriptionUsageSessionRows`\n */\nfunction formatSubscriptionUsageLimit(\n    limit: HarnessSubscriptionUsage['limits'][number],\n    currentTimeMs: number,\n): string {\n    const remainingPercentage = Math.round(Math.max(0, Math.min(100, 100 - limit.usedPercentage)));\n    const remainingPercentageColor = resolveRemainingPercentageColor(remainingPercentage);\n    const resetText = formatSubscriptionUsageReset(limit.resetsAt, currentTimeMs);\n    const label = limit.label.trim() || SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_SESSION_LABEL;\n\n    return [\n        colors.bold(label),\n        remainingPercentageColor(`${remainingPercentage}% remaining`),\n        ...(resetText ? {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cf9NnWiHG2SWftzZ3e5wJ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01D2anrMtsN4CceXHNhSn3L5","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\ai\\promptbook\\..\\..\\..\\.claude\\projects\\C--Users-me-work-ai-promptbook\\memory\\ptbk-coder-live-usage-task.md","content":"---\nname: ptbk-coder-live-usage-task\ndescription: Recurring \"[✨🍔] Show the usage of `ptbk coder` in real-time not freezed on each prompt\" task — IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-17 in commit d6cd92c16; check HEAD/working tree before re-implementing\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nRecurring prompt **\"[✨🍔] Show the usage of `ptbk coder` in real-time not freezed on each prompt / Refresh the usage percentages each 5s\"** was **fully IMPLEMENTED on 2026-09-17** in commit `d6cd92c16`, and `prompts/2026-09-0310-ptbk-coder-usage-update.md` is already marked `[x]`. Verify HEAD + working tree before writing any code — like [[agents-server-project-card-task]] and [[ptbk-coder-harness-install-method-task]], this one arrives already done.\n\n**The misleading pointer:** the prompt says \"You are working with [`ptbk coder`](src/cli/cli-commands/coder/run.ts)\", but that file is only a Commander shim — it builds `runOptions` and dynamically imports `scripts/run-codex-prompts/main/runCodexPrompts`. **All real coder work lives in `scripts/run-codex-prompts/`, not `src/cli/cli-commands/coder/`.** Grepping `src/cli/cli-commands/coder` for \"usage\" finds only `ping.ts` and looks like the feature is missing.\n\n**What the implementation looks like (choke points):**\n\n- `ui/startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh.ts` — the single refresher. `CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 5 * 1000`, fires once immediately, `isRefreshing` guard so ticks never overlap, `interval.unref()` so it can't keep the process alive. Started once at `runCodexPrompts.ts:145` (outside the prompt loop, after `resolvePromptRunner`), stopped at `:341`.\n- `ui/refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage.ts` is the only caller of `runner.getSubscriptionUsage()` — the old once-per-prompt read was removed, so DRY is already satisfied. Don't add a second read site.\n- Per-harness freshness differs: `OpenAiCodexRunner.getSubscriptionUsage()` spawns a short-lived `codex app-server` JSON-RPC helper on **every** call (fresh each read, but it is a process spawn every 5s for the whole run). `ClaudeCodeRunner` instead caches a snapshot updated from `rate_limit_event` lines of the **live** stream via `onOutputLine`.\n\n**Two traps when auditing whether it really works:**\n\n1. `onOutputLine` looks unthreaded for Claude Code — grepping `runGoScript/*.ts` shows it in `$runGoScriptUntilMarkerIdle.ts` but **not** in `$runGoScriptWithOutput.ts` (which is what `ClaudeCodeRunner` calls). It is fine: `$runGoScriptWithOutput` passes `{...options}` through to `runBashScriptWithOutput`, so the callback rides the spread.\n2. The frame is *not* gated by the phase timer. `getCoderRunUiAutoRefreshInterval` only auto-refreshes in `initializing/loading/running/verifying`, so a `waiting` phase looks like it would freeze the Usage rows — but `CoderRunUiState.setSubscriptionUsage()` calls `emitChange()`, which re-renders on every new snapshot regardless of phase. (Reset countdowns recompute from `Date.now()` in `buildSubscriptionUsageSessionRows`.)\n\nLanding page and changelog were updated too: `apps/coder-landing/src/data/advancedFeatures.ts` + `specs/sections/advanced-features.md`, feature 11 \"Pacing and retries\" (see [[coder-landing-terminal-grid-task]] for that app). Tests: `startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh.test.ts`, `refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage.test.ts`, `ClaudeCodeRunner.test.ts`, `createScriptOutputLineReader.test.ts` — 19 tests, all passing as of 2026-09-17.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":533,"cache_read_input_tokens":70962,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":533},"output_tokens":14,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"16bbd1a0-fdb9-4301-b22a-bed2255d0f09","uuid":"a3a54b2f-89b8-485d-9f70-a1a33f2b8663","timestamp":"2026-09-17T17:06:07.454Z","request_id":"req_011Cf9NnWFzHPCmEo9SWYwTG"}

Verify HEAD + working tree before writing any code — like [[agents-server-project-card-task]] and [[ptbk-coder-harness-install-method-task]], this one arrives already done.\n\n**The misleading pointer:** the prompt says \"You are working with [`ptbk coder`](src/cli/cli-commands/coder/run.ts)\", but that file is only a Commander shim — it builds `runOptions` and dynamically imports `scripts/run-codex-prompts/main/runCodexPrompts`. **All real coder work lives in `scripts/run-codex-prompts/`, not `src/cli/cli-commands/coder/`.** Grepping `src/cli/cli-commands/coder` for \"usage\" finds only `ping.ts` and looks like the feature is missing.\n\n**What the implementation looks like (choke points):**\n\n- `ui/startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh.ts` — the single refresher. `CODER_RUN_SUBSCRIPTION_USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 5 * 1000`, fires once immediately, `isRefreshing` guard so ticks never overlap, `interval.unref()` so it can't keep the process alive. Started once at `runCodexPrompts.ts:145` (outside the prompt loop, after `resolvePromptRunner`), stopped at `:341`.\n- `ui/refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage.ts` is the only caller of `runner.getSubscriptionUsage()` — the old once-per-prompt read was removed, so DRY is already satisfied. Don't add a second read site.\n- Per-harness freshness differs: `OpenAiCodexRunner.getSubscriptionUsage()` spawns a short-lived `codex app-server` JSON-RPC helper on **every** call (fresh each read, but it is a process spawn every 5s for the whole run). `ClaudeCodeRunner` instead caches a snapshot updated from `rate_limit_event` lines of the **live** stream via `onOutputLine`.\n\n**Two traps when auditing whether it really works:**\n\n1. `onOutputLine` looks unthreaded for Claude Code — grepping `runGoScript/*.ts` shows it in `$runGoScriptUntilMarkerIdle.ts` but **not** in `$runGoScriptWithOutput.ts` (which is what `ClaudeCodeRunner` calls). It is fine: `$runGoScriptWithOutput` passes `{...options}` through to `runBashScriptWithOutput`, so the callback rides the spread.\n2. The frame is *not* gated by the phase timer. `getCoderRunUiAutoRefreshInterval` only auto-refreshes in `initializing/loading/running/verifying`, so a `waiting` phase looks like it would freeze the Usage rows — but `CoderRunUiState.setSubscriptionUsage()` calls `emitChange()`, which re-renders on every new snapshot regardless of phase. (Reset countdowns recompute from `Date.now()` in `buildSubscriptionUsageSessionRows`.)\n\nLanding page and changelog were updated too: `apps/coder-landing/src/data/advancedFeatures.ts` + `specs/sections/advanced-features.md`, feature 11 \"Pacing and retries\" (see [[coder-landing-terminal-grid-task]] for that app). Tests: `startCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsageRefresh.test.ts`, `refreshCoderRunUiSubscriptionUsage.test.ts`, `ClaudeCodeRunner.test.ts`, `createScriptOutputLineReader.test.ts` — 19 tests, all passing as of 2026-09-17.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false,"memdirStamped":true}}

includes the diagnostic recipe and the on-box recovery steps\n- [Agents Server implicit FROM @Adam task](agents-server-implicit-from-adam-task.md) — recurring \"[✨🟥] Every agent should implicitly inherit from `@Adam`\": the inheritance code was always right; root cause (found 2026-08-21) was `getAgentPermanentId` resolving a name to a **soft-deleted namesake** after a core agent was reinstated — plus how to diagnose \"works locally, broken on live\" via public routes\n- [Agents Server projects default-running task](agents-server-projects-default-running-task.md) — recurring \"default state of the agent project should be running\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-19 via `desired-states.json` (absent = running) + boot/5-min autostart pass; nginx resolves project ports per request so apply-domains only runs when a domain actually changes\n- [Agents Server project card task](agents-server-project-card-task.md) — recurring \"project card with nice title and icon\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-07 (check working tree first); resolve in createAgentProjectInfo only; favicon route is login-gated and SSR img errors are lost before hydration\n- [Goal-chat planned messages task](agents-server-goal-chat-planned-messages-task.md) — recurring \"agent says he planned a message but there are none\" / \"should work like setInterval\": planning goes via the `messages/planned/<message>.json` sidecar (AgentKit `set_timeout` tools are dead code) and planned messages now repeat by re-arming the same timeout row in place\n- [ptbk coder --git-changes task](ptbk-coder-git-changes-task.md) — \"[✨🛼] Allow to pick what happen with dirty working dir\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-29 (`--ignore-git-changes` removed); the three traps = shared `addPromptRunnerExecutionOptions`, the dead `createCoderRunOptionsForAgent` bridge, and the `[^]` line being rewritten every step\n- [ptbk coder prompt-checkbox task](ptbk-coder-prompt-checkbox-task.md) — recurring \"[✨🤺] allow prompts with no `[ ]`\": round 1 (unmarked = todo) + round 2 (`[.]` alias, `ptbk-coder-ignore`); choke points are `parsePromptFile` + `loadPromptFiles`, and the ignore marker is own-line only so the prompt file that documents it does not ignore itself\n- [ptbk coder harness install-method task](ptbk-coder-harness-install-method-task.md) — \"[✨🕗] ptbk coder npm-updates a standalone Codex\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-04 (check working tree first); choke points = `HarnessDefinition.standaloneInstallation` + `resolveHarnessInstallationMethodFromPaths` + `resolveHarnessUpdatePlan`; `unknown` never falls back to npm; probe real origins via a throwaway jest test, not ts-node\n- [ptbk coder init no-override task](ptbk-coder-init-no-override-task.md) — \"[✨🤲] coder init overrides scripts in `package.json`/`settings.json`\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-11; single choke point is `mergeStringRecordJsonFile` (now additive-only + returns `addedEntryKeys`), plus the referenced-artifact model that creates `developer.book`/`AGENTS.md`/`common.md` only with the script that points at them\n- [ptbk coder qwen-code harness task](ptbk-coder-qwen-code-harness-task.md) — \"[✨🆓] Add `qwen-code` harness\": IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-02; adding any harness is driven by `CLI_AGENT_HARNESS_NAMES` alone, the `qwen` CLI has **no** reasoning-effort flag (so `--thinking-level` is not forwarded, like `gemini`), and `.vscode/terminals.json` is permission-gated so the agent cannot edit it\n- [Promptbook prettier baseline](promptbook-prettier-baseline.md) — repo is NOT clean under its declared prettier 2.8.8; don't chase `prettier --check` failures on files you didn't touch\n- [Verification step order](promptbook-verification-step-order.md) — `test-for-ptbk-coder` = 10 ordered steps, aborts at first failure; a `test-unit` failure leaves agents-server lint + Next build unrun; suite-wall-clock≈whole-run timeout = suspended host, not a regression\n- [Jest EPERM verification flake](promptbook-jest-eperm-verification-flake.md) — `test-for-ptbk-coder` dying at `test-unit` with `kill EPERM` after all tests pass is environmental (Windows teardown), not your diff; fixed via `scripts/ignore-kill-eperm.js` preload\n- [Coder bash login-shell cost](coder-bash-login-shell-cost.md) — `bash -lc` costs ~9.5s here (nvm in `~/.bash_profile`) and `-l` is load-bearing for harness PATH; budget coder-test setup waits separately from the asserted behavior\n- [Agents Server show-progress task](agents-server-show-progress-task.md) — recurring \"show real progress of the agent\" chat prompt: runner is a separate process, the only live signal is its stream-json runtime log on the shared folder; wire via resolveAgentMessageRuntimeActivity → progressCard (never static/fake text)\n- [Agents Server System-menu warnings gating](agents-server-system-warnings-gating.md) — resolveHeaderSystemWarnings choke point gates admin-only ⚠️ (resource/core-agents/Shibboleth); the terminal is ~654px tall at every viewport, so balance the hero by growing the copy\n- [Codex ChatGPT task-details task](codex-chatgpt-task-details-task.md) — recurring \"[✨😺] codex ChatGPT vs API key\" prompt: TRUE root cause was `codex login status` printing to stderr while detection used `2>/dev/null` (fix: `2>&1` in buildCodexScript.ts + install.sh); earlier attempts only did the display sidecar chain\n- [Codex harness-auth wizard task](codex-harness-auth-wizard-task.md) — recurring \"[✨👥] Fix the OpenAI Codex authentication\" (/admin/harness-auth): root cause bare `codex` TUI in `resolve_runner_authentication_command`; fix = `codex login --device-auth` + sign-in wizard + current-method detection\n- [Chat source-chip display task](chat-source-chip-display-task.md) — recurring \"[✨🙍] Show the sources in some nicer way\": fix `resolveCitationSourceDisplay.ts` (single choke point for label+icon), NOT the agents-server resolver (returns null for non-URL sources)\n- [Agents Server admin menu wiring](agents-server-admin-menu-wiring.md) — how to add a System-menu admin page: buildHeaderSystemMenuItems + globally-unique-icon test, 3-place translations, super-admin gating; extends vps-domains-certificates-task\n- [Agents Server self-update task](agents-server-self-update-task.md) — recurring \"[✨🏖] Fix the self-update\": panel runs the DEPLOYED release's install.sh (repo fixes arrive one update late); routing choke point resolveLocalSqliteTableLocation\n- [Task-manager sort-by-finished task](task-manager-sort-by-finished-task.md) — recurring \"[✨🆗] tasks in task manager sorted by finished time\": ALREADY fixed (commit 0ab5ede20); fix = runDurableUserChatJobWorkerTick fans coordinator poll across all servers via serverContextOverride; plus VPS-wide read-only task manager (/admin/task-manager-vps)\n- [Task-manager page-links task](task-manager-page-links-task.md) — recurring \"link task manager tasks to their page/chat + reverse\": detail pages & chat-history→task reverse ALREADY existed; real gap = forward link (task→page) via shared adminChatTaskLinks.resolveAdminChatTaskTargetLink\n- [Stalwart email server task](stalwart-email-server-task.md) — 6 confirmed root causes (JMAP `/jmap/` endpoint, collection props are objects not arrays, `promptbook.invalid` aborted the installer, bootstrap probing;
